recipes.title: Shawarma Baharāt or Baharat Shawarma
ingredients: Cayenne or chilli powder — to taste (optional)
For chicken shawarma, reduce the cloves and nutmeg slightly and increase the paprika.
For lamb or beef, keep it bold — use the full blend as above.
Shawarma Spice Mix used mainly for chicken
steps: Whisk the spices: Put all the spices in a bowl and whisk together well, breaking up any lumps of onion powder.
Store: Bag it up or put it in a storage container with a couple of silica gel packets. As it's all powdered spices, it is shelf stable and keeps for quite some time.
Use: Best on grilled beef or lamb. It works on chicken, but the channel's separate shawarma mix suits chicken better.

recipes.title: Shawarma Spice Mix
ingredients: Smoked paprika (or sweet paprika) — 2 tsp / 4 g
Ground turmeric — 1½ tsp / 3 g (omit if you want Baharat-style)
Ground black pepper — ½ tsp / 1 g
Cayenne pepper — ½ tsp / 1 g (adjust to taste)
Salt — 1 tsp / 5 g (optional — or add separately when using)
This mix is used mainly for chicken; Baharat-style shawarma seasoning is used more for beef and lamb
Shawarma-style marinade: 2½ to 3 tablespoons spice mix per 1 kg chicken
Dry rub only: 2 to 2¼ tbsp per 1 kg chicken
steps: Mix the spices: Put all of the spices into a bowl and mix them. The host does not measure each one on camera; the amounts are in the description. Sumac is optional — it adds a sour element so you don't have to use lime or lemon.
Store: Tip the mix into a bag and add a silica gel sachet so it stays shelf-stable.

To use (from the description): This mix is used mainly for chicken; a Baharat-style shawarma seasoning (turmeric omitted) is used more for beef and lamb. For a shawarma-style marinade, 2½ to 3 tablespoons of spice mix per 1 kg chicken. As a dry rub only, 2 to 2¼ tbsp per 1 kg chicken.

recipes.title: Mango Passionfruit Jam Recipe - Bold & Bright!
ingredients: Mango flesh, ripe, diced — 4 cups (3⅓ UK cups / 900 g)
Passionfruit pulp, with seeds — 2½ cups (550 g)
Powdered pectin (standard type) — 1 standard pack (50 g) or 2½ tbsp (18–20 g)
If using liquid pectin (from the description):
1 standard pack of powdered pectin (about 50 g) is about 1 pouch (3 oz / 85 ml) of liquid pectin
Use 85 ml (1 pouch or about ⅓ cup) of liquid pectin, added at the end after the fruit and sugar have boiled
steps: Prep the fruit: Cut the passion fruit in half and scoop out all the flesh and seeds. Skin the mango, cut down the sides of the long flat stone, and roughly cube the flesh — it will break down as it boils. For this recipe the host wants about a kilo of mango (the description lists 900 g / 4 cups).
Mix the pectin with some of the sugar: Stir some of the sugar into the powdered pectin so the pectin does not clump when it goes into the pan.
Start the pan: Put the mango, passion fruit, lemon juice and a little salt in the pan (the host says salt enhances the taste). Set a nice medium flame, bring it up towards a simmer, then to a boil.
Rolling boil: It needs to come to a rolling boil that does not stop when you stir. Boil quite hard for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring so the sugars do not catch on the bottom, then turn it off.
Set test: The host uses a cold plate from the fridge: put a little jam on the plate; if it sets and wrinkles, it is ready.
Jar while hot: Spoon into sterilised jars and wipe any spills on the rims.

Water bath: Stand the jars on a trivet in a pan, cover them with water, and boil for 10 minutes. Take them out and let them go cold. The host says the sealed jars will be shelf-stable for one year. If you use liquid pectin instead of powdered, the description says to boil the fruit, sugar, lemon juice and salt first, stir in the liquid pectin off the heat, then bring it back to a full rolling boil for 1–2 minutes before jarring.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3iQa2kAfRW0

recipes.title: British pork sausage BANGER with BUTCHERS Rusk
ingredients: Ice-cold water — 600 ml (approx. 2.5 UK cups / 2.5 US cups)
Optional: mace or allspice — 1 tsp (for depth). I used allspice
Sausage casings — natural hog casings, rinsed and soaked or collagen casings
HOW TO MAKE BUTCHER'S RUSK VIDEO BEFORE THIS ONE -
Casing size I left that open to choice — Standard collagen casings used for British-style sausages (like Cumberland, Lincolnshire, or traditional bangers) are typically:
28–30 mm: Gives a slightly thinner sausage, used for chipolatas or breakfast-style bangers.
30–32 mm: Most common size for traditional British bangers and Cumberland sausages.
These sizes refer to the stuffed diameter, not the flat width.
Edible collagen casings are usually used for fresh sausages. I used the 28 Best, Rik
Salt Analysis per Kilogram of Meat
That’s 15 g of salt per 1 kg of meat mixture
This 5% salt-to-rusk ratio and 1.5% salt-to-meat ratio is standard for traditional British sausage making, where:
1.5–1.8% salt per kg of meat is typical
The FSA (UK Food Standards Agency) recommends a maximum of ~1.13 g of salt per 100 g of sausage for health, but artisan butchers often exceed this for flavour, texture, and preservation.
If targeting reduced sodium or home cook audience:
Many now aim for 1.2% or even 1% for lighter seasoning
steps: Mix the spices: Combine the white pepper, black pepper, sage, salt, coriander, allspice (optional) and nutmeg with the dextrose (or sugar) so they're evenly mixed before going into the meat.

Mix the sausage meat: Mix the pork mince with the dry butcher's rusk and the spice mix by hand. Gradually add the fridge-cold (or ice-cold) water and keep mixing until the meat turns tacky as the rusk rehydrates.
Rest overnight: Divide into zip-lock bags and refrigerate overnight so the flavours develop.

Stuff: Pack the meat tightly into a sausage stuffer, fit the nozzle and feed collagen (or natural) casings on. Let the meat push through with gentle, natural pressure while you hold the casing, avoiding air pockets and not filling it too tight.
Rest the casings: Refrigerate the coiled sausage overnight so the casings soften, which makes them easier to twist.
Link: Pinch and twist into individual sausages, or fold the length in half and twist and loop it through to form links. Tying the ends is optional.
Cook: Fry in a pan with a little water and a splash of oil until cooked through and browned. Serve with HP sauce.

recipes.title: Butcher’s Rusk KEY ingredient for SAUSAGE MAKING
ingredients: Plain (all-purpose) flour — 500 g (3⅓ UK cups / 4 US cups), plus 50 g for evaporation (see the note in the description)
Baking powder — 10 g (2 tsp; the description also lists 1 US tsp)

The host makes a kilo batch in the video: 1 kg flour plus 100 g extra for evaporation, with salt and baking powder mixed in. Scale the description amounts to match the batch you are making; do not invent extra quantities.
steps: Heat the oven: The description says to preheat to 200°C (400°F) fan / 220°C (430°F) conventional / Gas 7. The host says this is a two-part cook, so have the oven on at the start.

Mix the dough: The description lists a 500 g flour batch (plus 50 g extra flour in the note for evaporation) with 10 g salt, 10 g baking powder and 300 ml cold water. In the video the host makes a kilo of rusk: a 1 kg bag of flour plus 100 g extra, because moisture will evaporate in the oven and you should end up with roughly a kilo. Mix in the salt and baking powder, add the water, and knead for a couple of minutes until it comes together.

Shape and first bake: Put the dough on a parchment-lined tray and flatten it. Some say about 1½ cm thick; the host says it doesn't matter because it will be baked twice. Bake about 35 minutes (the description says 30–35 minutes) until firm and golden. It will be quite hard on top. Take it out and let it go completely cold.

Second bake: Heat the oven to 100°C (the description gives 100–120°C / 210–250°F). Break the loaf into chunks so it dries and is easier to blend later. Bake about 1½ to 2 hours (the description says to turn occasionally) until completely dry and crisp.
Cool and grind: Let it cool completely, then blend it as fine as you like in a food processor — it will absorb water in sausages, so the grind is up to you.
Dry and store: Because the blender warms the crumbs, tip them out and air-dry an hour or two, turning them once. Store in airtight bags with a couple of silica gel sachets to keep the moisture out.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9NIEq5qyur8
Uploaded 2025-06-29.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F) fan / 220°C (430°F) conventional / Gas 7; Reduce oven to 100–120°C (210–250°F); Bake for 1½ to 2 hours, turning occasionally, until completely dry and crisp.

recipes.title: Imitation Vanilla Extract - Make Your Own Vanilla Essence Without Alcohol or Beans
ingredients: Ethyl vanillin — 0.3 grams (approx. 1/8 tsp or 2 pinches)
(or use homemade caramel colouring — see below)
Distilled or filtered water — 500 ml (2 US cups / 1.75 UK cups)
Thanks to potassium sorbate, it should keep for 6–12 months at room temperature. Shake before use.
steps: Dissolve the vanillin: Put about 100 ml of the water in a jug, add the vanillin powder and the ethyl vanillin (the stronger of the two), and stir until fully dissolved; there's no rush.
Add colour and preservative: Stir in the caramel colour (about half a teaspoon gives the familiar colour) and the potassium sorbate preservative.
Top up: Mix with the rest of the water to make half a litre and bottle it.
Store and use: Kept in a dark, cool cupboard it lasts 6–12 months. Use exactly as you would shop-bought vanilla.

recipes.title: COUNTRY fried PORK CHOPS with BACON GRAVY
ingredients: 4 boneless pork loin chops (about 200–250 g / 7–9 oz each)
60 ml (4 tbsp / ¼ US cup) vegetable oil, for frying
1 tbsp (8 g) cornstarch or semolina in the flour mix
½ tsp (2.5 g) salt (adjust to taste)
Optional: a pinch of cayenne or mustard powder for depth
steps: Make buttermilk: If you don't have buttermilk, stir 1 tablespoon of apple cider vinegar (or other vinegar or lemon juice) into each cup of milk. About 2 cups were used here. Leave 5 minutes to curdle.
Marinate: Submerge the pork chops (cut from pork loin) in the buttermilk, cover and leave for about 4 hours.
Season the flour: Mix the flour with salt, about ½ teaspoon of paprika, garlic powder and onion powder, plus cornflour or semolina for extra crunch if you like.
Dredge and rest: Lift the chops from the buttermilk, give them a shake, coat well in the seasoned flour and rest on a rack for 10 minutes so the coating sticks.
Fry: Shallow fry in hot oil for about 4–5 minutes per side, turning more than once. Keep warm on the rack, then pour off the oil and the burnt flour bits.
Crisp the bacon: Using a little of the oil, fry the chopped bacon as crisp as you like, then remove it.

Make the gravy: Stir a couple of tablespoons of flour into the fat (with the butter from the ingredient list) and cook out the rawness. Season lightly with salt and black pepper, add a teaspoon of mustard (optional), then pour in all the milk and stir gently until smooth. Thin with a little milk or water if too thick, then return the bacon and its fat. Cheese can be added too.
Serve: Serve the chops on mashed potato with the bacon gravy spooned over, and English mustard on the side if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xHToV8NqUfQ

recipes.title: COSORI TwinFry Air Fryer - Layered Mince & Potato Pie
ingredients: 1 beef stock cube in 150 ml hot water
¼ head white or Savoy cabbage, cut into 2–3 thick wedges
Temp: 170°C / 340°F — I cooked at 160°C / 320°F and upped the temp.
Cover with foil for the first 20 mins (especially if pastry lid), uncover to brown
Basket B – Garlic Butter Cabbage Wedges:
Mix melted butter, garlic, salt, and pepper
Temp: 170°C / 340°F — I cooked at 160°C / 320°F and upped the temp.
Flip once halfway for golden edges
steps: Parboil the potatoes: Peel 2 medium potatoes (300–350 g total), and boil them 8 minutes only, then drain. Toss or brush with a little oil or melted butter and ½ tsp salt when you layer them.

Filling: Cook the diced onion and minced garlic to take the rawness out, then brown the minced beef (400 g). Stir in about a tablespoon of tomato purée (the description lists 2 tsp) and cook out the sourness, then a little beef stock (a stock cube in 150 ml hot water — the host uses a minimal amount of gravy), Worcestershire sauce, dried thyme, salt and pepper. Flour (1½ tsp in the description) is optional if you need it thicker; the host didn't think he needed it this time. Let the filling cool a little.

Line the tin: Roll shortcrust pastry (ready-made or homemade) and line a 7-inch springform tin. Layer in the mince filling and the potato. If you add a pastry lid, the notes say to cover with foil for the first 20 minutes so it doesn't over-brown. The captions are clearer about rolling the pastry than about every layer order; watch the video for that rather than inventing it.

Bake: In the air fryer, use bake mode at 160–170°C (320–340°F) — the host started at 160°C — for about 35–40 minutes. It can also be made in a regular oven; no oven time is given in the captions, so don't invent one. Rest about 5 minutes before you cut it.

Garlic-butter cabbage (optional side): Cut ¼ head of white or Savoy cabbage into 2–3 thick wedges. Brush with melted butter mixed with minced garlic, salt and pepper. Bake in the other air-fryer basket at the same temperature 30–35 minutes, flipping halfway for golden edges.

recipes.title: CREAMY CHICKEN Taquitos Oven-Baked WEEKNIGHT Favourite
ingredients: ½ cup (60g / 2 oz) shredded cheddar cheese
¼ cup (60ml / 4 tbsp) salsa (mild or spicy, your choice) see note below
10 small flour or corn tortillas (15–18 cm / 6–7 inch)
Olive oil or cooking spray for brushing
steps: Warm the tortillas: Sprinkle the tortillas with a little water, wrap them loosely and put them in the oven for about 5 minutes to freshen up.

Make the filling: Season the softened cream cheese with pepper, salt, garlic powder and onion powder and mix, then add the cumin and the shredded cooked chicken. Mix in the cheddar, then a little salsa (a homemade jalapeño sauce was used) to make a nice loose mix.
Roll: Spoon some filling along each tortilla, fold in and roll up tightly.
Oil and bake: Brush a little olive oil on the tray where the rolls will sit, place them seam side down, brush a little more oil on top, and bake for about 15 minutes until blistered and crispy.
Serve: Let them cool for a minute so they crisp up (they are very hot inside), then serve with more jalapeño sauce.

recipes.title: Zesty Jalapeño Lime Hot Sauce
ingredients: 10 fresh jalapeño peppers (about 250 g / 8.8 oz), stemmed and roughly chopped
Red chilli flakes (optional) for red specks
CREAMY CHICKEN Taquitos Oven-Baked USING THIS SAUCE:
steps: Garlic and lime: Mash and roughly chop the garlic and put it in a blender with the juice of two limes.
Prep the jalapeños: Remove the stalks, seeds and cores from about 10 jalapeños (seeds are optional, but they get stuck in your teeth) and dice them roughly to help the blender.

Add the rest: Add the red chilli flakes (Korean flakes used here for red specks), the vinegar (with the water from the ingredient list), olive oil, salt, sugar and about ¼ teaspoon of citric acid for a longer shelf life.
Blend: Blend until smooth, or blend less if you want some texture.
Cook: Pour into a pan, bring it up to a simmer over a medium heat and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring so nothing catches.
Cool and bottle: Turn off the heat, let it cool completely and bottle it. It's a fresh sauce: about 2 weeks in the fridge without citric acid, about 4 weeks with it.

recipes.title: BLACK FOREST Fairy Cakes - like Black Forest Gâteau in one bite
ingredients: Butter (softened): 115g | 8 tbsp | ½ UK cup | ½ US cup
Caster sugar: 115g | 9 tbsp | ½ UK cup | ½ US cup
Self-raising flour: 115g | 8½ tbsp | ¾ UK cup | ¾ US cup
Cocoa powder (unsweetened): 25g | 2½ tbsp | ¼ UK cup | ¼ US cup
Milk: 1–2 tbsp | 15–30ml | 1–2 UK tbsp | 1–2 US tbsp
Cherry jam or morello cherry conserve: ~6 tsp | 120g
Double cream (heavy cream): 150ml | 10 tbsp | ⅔ UK cup | ⅔ US cup
steps: Make the sponge: Heat the oven to 180°C (the description also gives 160°C fan / 350°F / Gas 4). Cream the softened butter and caster sugar with a little salt. Beat in the eggs, adding a couple of tablespoons of the flour first so they don't curdle, then the rest of the self-raising flour, cocoa, 1 teaspoon of instant coffee, the milk (1–2 tbsp) and vanilla if you are using it.
Bake: Spoon the mix into bun cases and bake 15–18 minutes, until done. Cool.

Fill and top: The description has cherry jam or morello cherry conserve, and cream sweetened with 1 tbsp icing sugar, optionally stabilised with 1 tsp powdered gelatine bloomed in 1 tbsp cold water. The host mentions cherry brandy in the cream or jam — skip that if children will eat them. Core or slice a lid, add jam and cream, replace the lid, and finish with more cream and a cherry. Optional dark chocolate shavings go on top. Don't expect the cream to sit for a long time if it is not stabilised.

recipes.title: OLD School FRANKS and BEANS That Taste Like Childhood ELEVATED
ingredients: Canned baked beans — 2 cans (800g / 28 oz total)
Brown sugar — 1 tbsp | 15g | 0.05 UK cup | 0.06 US cup
steps: Prep: Dice the onion and chop the frankfurters into pieces (any size of frank works).
Soften the onion: Melt the butter and sauté the onion until soft (colour is fine), seasoning with pepper only. The beans, franks and sauces bring enough salt.
Brown the franks: Add the franks and stir-fry until they take some colour and start to split.
Add the flavourings: Stir in the brown sugar, a couple of tablespoons of ketchup, about a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce, the yellow mustard and the smoked paprika (optional).
Simmer with the beans: Add the baked beans and simmer about 10 minutes so the flavours come together.

Serve: Serve on hot buttered toast, with rice or mash, or in a bowl with crusty bread. For the elevated version, butter thick toast, top it with franks and beans and mozzarella, and bake until the cheese melts.

recipes.title: AUSSIE CHICKEN Parmi (No Parmesan, No Fuss) Might be the BEST PARM In the World!
ingredients: 2 tbsp plain flour | 15 g | 1 UK tbsp + 1 US tbsp
50 g dried breadcrumbs | ½ US cup | ⅓ UK cup
2 tbsp vegetable oil | 30 ml (for shallow frying)
200 ml tomato passata / marinara | 200 g | ¾ US cup + 1 tbsp | ¾ UK cup
2-3 slices ham (round or shaved) I usedd smoked for more flavour
100 g shredded mozzarella | 1 US cup | ¾ UK cup
steps: Make the tomato sauce: Gently cook the minced garlic in a touch of olive oil with a little salt, then stir in the passata or marinara and the dried oregano. Simmer a minute or so until thick enough to cling to the chicken. Taste shop-bought sauce and add the sugar if it is sour. Let it cool.

Prepare the chicken: Trim off the loose tenderloin and any bits of bone. Butterfly each breast from the thick end without cutting all the way through, then pound it lightly under a bag to an even thickness. Season with salt, plus oregano and garlic powder (optional).
Crumb: Dust the chicken in flour, dip it in beaten egg, then press it into breadcrumbs. Rest it on a rack for 10 minutes so the coating sticks.
Fry: Heat enough oil in a pan and shallow-fry the schnitzels one at a time over a moderate heat, turning as often as needed, until golden and cooked through.
Top: Cover each schnitzel with ham, filling in the gaps, so it stops the crumb going soggy. Spread over a good helping of tomato sauce and top with mozzarella.
Melt and serve: Put it under the grill until the cheese melts and colours. Serve with hot chips and salad.

recipes.title: Strawberry, Red Onion & Ginger Relish
ingredients: Fresh strawberries — 250g | 1¾ cups (US/UK), hulled and chopped
Red onion — 1 small (approx. 100g) | ½ cup finely chopped
Fresh ginger — 1 tbsp | 15g | 3 tsp, finely grated
Brown sugar — 2 tbsp | 30g | 1½ tbsp (UK), packed – more if using sour strawberries -
Optional: pinch of chilli flakes for heat
Store in the fridge for up to 10 days. Flavour improves after a day.
steps: Prep: Wash, hull and rough-chop the strawberries (at least about 250 g; ripe, under-ripe or overripe all work). Finely dice the red onion and grate about a tablespoon of fresh ginger.

Soften the aromatics: With no butter or oil, put a splash of the vinegar in a stainless pan with the onion and ginger. Add the salt and black pepper and sauté on a low flame for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until softened and the liquid has gone. A little colour is fine, but don't burn them.

Add the fruit: Stir in the strawberries and about 2 tablespoons of brown sugar (white works too), the optional chilli flakes, and the rest of the apple cider vinegar to make about 3 tablespoons in total.

Simmer uncovered: Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered, stirring so nothing catches, for about 10–15 minutes (it can take 20–25 depending on your pan), until jammy but with bits of strawberry still in it. Taste and adjust the seasoning along the way.

Finish: Turn the heat off once it is a little thinner than you want, because it thickens slightly as it cools. Serve with strong cheddar, on cheese on toast, or with cold meats. It keeps about 10 days in the fridge.

From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RCezD_G25bE

recipes.title: Strawberry Shortcake From British Origins to American Summertime Favourite
ingredients: Fresh strawberries — 450g (1 lb), hulled and sliced
steps: Dry mix: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Stir together the flour, 2 teaspoons of baking powder, the salt and the sugar.
Rub in the butter: Rub the butter in until it looks like breadcrumbs. It doesn't need to be very cold.
Add the cream: Stir in the vanilla and cream just until it forms a loose dough. Don't overmix.
Shape: Turn it onto a floured counter and bring it together lightly so it stays flaky; cracks are fine. Pat it down to no thinner than 1 inch and cut out rounds.

Top and bake: Put them on a lined baking tray, brush the tops with cream and sprinkle with sugar (the host uses caramel granulated sugar; demerara or plain granulated also works). Bake 12–15 minutes until golden, then cool on a rack.
Macerate the strawberries: Hull the strawberries, slice them fairly thickly and stir them with the sugar and a very small pinch of salt. Leave them to release their juices.
Whip the cream: Whip 240 ml of cream with a tablespoon of icing sugar and a dash of vanilla.
Assemble: Split each shortcake, spoon some strawberry juice and strawberries onto the bottom, add whipped cream, and put the top back on.

recipes.title: Ultimate Chicken Lasagna with Italian Herb White Sauce
ingredients: 1 tsp onion powder — of use 2 cloves garlic minced
½ tsp dried thyme or Italian seasoning
Salt and white pepper to taste
500 g (3 US cups / 3 UK cups) cooked, shredded or diced chicken
200–250 g (7–9 oz) fresh spinach or 150–200 g (5–7 oz) frozen spinach - or more!
150 g (1½ US cups / 1½ UK cups) grated mozzarella
100 g (1 US cup / 1 UK cup) grated cheddar or provolone
60 g (½ US cup / ½ UK cup) grated Parmesan
150 g (5 oz / ⅔ cup) ricotta or cottage cheese (optional)
1 tbsp fresh chopped parsley or basil (plus extra for garnish)
steps: Heat the oven and start the spinach: Put the oven on about 180°C (350°F). The dish is about 20 × 20. Sauté the spinach in a little olive oil or butter until it is down, with a pinch of nutmeg (and the optional lemon juice from the description). Season and set aside.
Season the chicken: Use cooked shredded or diced chicken — the host uses rotisserie. Mix it with a little Italian seasoning, black pepper and paprika from the list.

White sauce: Melt the butter, stir in the flour (a couple of tablespoons in the captions; the description lists 60 g / 4 tbsp) and onion powder, and cook the rawness out. Add the hot chicken stock (from a cube is fine) and the milk and cream from the description — the captions clearly mention the stock going in; they don't name the milk and cream as they go in, so follow the video for that moment rather than inventing a pouring order. Season with black or white pepper, and the optional mustard powder or nutmeg if you like. Cook until it thickens, but not too thick, because it has to go inside the lasagna. Turn off the heat.

Layer: In the dish, add pasta sheets (pre-cooked or no-boil; snap them to fit), more white sauce, the chicken, a little ricotta or cottage cheese if you are using it, spinach, mozzarella, mature cheddar or provolone, Parmesan, and a pinch of Italian seasoning or parsley. Repeat the layers, finishing with sauce and cheese.

Bake: Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes, then uncover and bake a further 15–20 minutes (the host also says about 20–25) until the top is golden and bubbling. Rest about 6 or 7 minutes before you cut it.

recipes.title: Beef and Onion Jam  the ultimate topping
ingredients: (Measurements in tsp / tbsp / grams / ml / UK & US cups)
1 tbsp (15 ml / 15g / 0.5 UK tbsp / 0.5 US tbsp) olive oil
1 tbsp (12g / 15 ml / 0.5 UK tbsp / 0.5 US tbsp) brown sugar
450g (1 lb / 2.5 UK cups / 2 US cups) ground beef (20% fat preferred)
1 tbsp (15 ml / 15g / 0.5 UK tbsp / 0.5 US tbsp) balsamic vinegar
1 tbsp (15 ml / 15g / 0.5 UK tbsp / 0.5 US tbsp) Worcestershire sauce
1 Crumbled beef cube — I used Oxo
1/2 tsp (2g) sea salt, or to taste
Optional: 1/4 tsp (1g) chilli flakes or smoked paprika
steps: Slice the onions: Slice the onions into roughly even slices so they caramelise at the same rate.
Soften: Put the onions in a pan with a little salt, the brown sugar and the oil. Cover with a lid and let them steam and soften, stirring now and then.
Caramelise: When most of the moisture has evaporated, take the lid off and keep cooking, watching that the sugar doesn't burn, until the onions caramelise.
Cook the beef: Push the onions to one side, add the beef mince, season with a little salt and pepper and cook, breaking it up, until there's no pink.
Sauces: Add about a tablespoon each of balsamic vinegar and Worcestershire sauce, and cook until any water from the meat has evaporated.
Spice and stock: Stir in chilli flakes (optional) and smoked or ordinary paprika, then crumble in half to one beef stock cube, depending on how beefy you want it.
Combine: Mix the caramelised onions back through the beef, then turn off the heat.
Store: Let it go completely cold, then tub it. Use within about 5–7 days in the fridge, or freeze for about 3 months.

recipes.title: OLD SCHOOL CHOCOLATE Sponge and MINT Custard CLASSIC UK school dessert
ingredients: Self-raising flour — 200g | 1⅓ UK cups | 1⅔ US cups | 13 tbsp | 16 tbsp

steps: Heat the oven: Put it on 180°C (160°C fan) / 350°F. Grease and line a rectangular tray — about 12 × 9 inches, or 13 × 9 if that's what you have.

recipes.title: QUICK and Savoury Black PEPPER CHICKEN Stir Fry
ingredients: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, thinly sliced — 450 g (1 lb)
Regular light soy sauce — 1 tbsp (15 ml)
Freshly ground black pepper, coarsely ground — 2 tsp (4 g)
Yellow onion, sliced — 1 large (the host used two small)
Button or cremini mushrooms, sliced — 200 g (2 cups)
Cornflour / cornstarch slurry — 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Marinate the chicken: Slice the chicken (the host uses breast here; the description allows thighs or breasts). Mix it with about 1 tablespoon light soy sauce, a good tablespoon of cornflour, and optionally a little of the black pepper and a little sesame oil. Leave about 15 minutes while you prep the vegetables. The whole dish comes together in about 30 minutes.

Prep the vegetables: Slice the mushrooms (the host used 370 g on this cook; the description lists 200 g / 2 cups), slice the onion, and cube or slice the red pepper. Slice the green onions into pieces about 1–2 cm long and keep them for garnish at the end.

Mix the sauce: Stir together about 1 tablespoon light soy sauce, 1 tablespoon dark soy sauce, 1 tablespoon oyster sauce (from the ingredient list), 1 tablespoon rice vinegar, a couple of tablespoons of sugar, and a couple of tablespoons of black pepper. The description lists 2 tsp pepper; the host also says that if the heat is too much you can bring it down to 1 tablespoon, as this is a black-pepper dish. Mix a cornflour slurry — 1 tablespoon cornflour with water (the description says 2 tbsp water) — and stir it again just before using, as it settles.
Cook the chicken: Heat a couple of tablespoons of oil in a pan. Cook the chicken first, tossing it for a couple of minutes until it has some cooking on it, then take it out.

Fry the aromatics and vegetables: Add a tad more oil if the pan is dry, then about a tablespoon of garlic and ginger (minced, or a paste of equal parts garlic and ginger with a little oil and water). Cook out a little of the rawness, then add the onion, pepper and mushrooms with a tad of salt to help draw moisture from the mushrooms. Don't cook the mushrooms too long if you want to keep some texture; they will cook down.

Sauce and thicken: Add the sauce. The host talks about the smell of the pepper, rice vinegar and a little sweetness. Stir in the cornflour slurry to thicken if you want. The captions are not explicit about the exact moment the cooked chicken goes back in after it was taken out; watch that moment in the video.

Finish and serve: Turn the flame off, stir through a good amount of the green onion (saving some for the top), and optionally a little sesame to dress it. The host says there is probably enough for about three good portions. Serve with rice, or whatever you like, and tone the pepper down to taste.

recipes.title: EASY Roasted Red Pepper and Tomato Soup with Cheddar Melt
ingredients: Tinned whole tomatoes, with juice — 1 can (400 g)
Dried thyme or basil — ½ tsp

Grated cheddar, mozzarella, or cheese of choice
steps: Roast the peppers and garlic: Roast 2 large red peppers with the garlic — the garlic will cook a lot faster than the peppers, so keep an eye on it. The captions don't give an oven temperature; watch the video rather than inventing one. When they're ready (the host talks about leaving them about 10 minutes at that stage, then peeling), take off the skins so you don't get black bits in the soup, and keep any roasting juices.

Start the soup: Dice the onion and sauté it in the olive oil with a tad of salt and pepper, not too high — you want it soft, not necessarily coloured. Add the roasted garlic and the peppers with their juices (chop if you like; everything will be blended). Tip in the tinned whole tomatoes and snip them with scissors, or use chopped tomatoes. Pour in the vegetable stock or water (500 ml in the description) and add optional smoked paprika, dried thyme or basil, and a pinch of sugar if you want.

Simmer and blend: Cook uncovered about 20 minutes so it intensifies and everything is soft, then blend until smooth. Finish with a little cream or coconut milk if you like (2 tbsp in the description). Season to taste. It freezes well in portions.

Cheddar melt: Mix softened butter with mayonnaise and spread it to the edges of the bread. Fill with grated cheddar, mozzarella or your cheese of choice and toast or grill until melted. Serve with the soup.

recipes.title: LEMON Drizzle OAT Loaf Cake - A Citrusy Tea Time Treat
ingredients: Rolled oats — 75 g | ½ UK cup | ¾ US cup
Milk — 120 ml | 4 fl oz | ½ UK cup | ½ US cup
Plain flour (all-purpose) — 150 g | 10 tbsp | 1¼ UK cups | 1¼ US cups
Butter (softened) — 115 g | 8 tbsp | ½ UK cup | ½ US cup
Caster sugar — 150 g | 8 tbsp | ¾ UK cup | ¾ US cup
Lemon juice — 60 ml | 4 tbsp | ¼ UK cup | ¼ US cup
Icing sugar — 100 g | 8 tbsp | ¾ UK cup | ¾ US cup
steps: Soak the oats: Pour the milk over the rolled oats and leave them for about 15 minutes, giving them a turn after about 10 minutes so they absorb the milk. Heat the oven to 170°C.

Prep the lemons and tin: While the oats soak, zest the lemons and squeeze the juice. Line a 2 lb loaf tin (or a slightly larger tin for a bigger cake; it may crack, which doesn't matter for a drizzle cake).
Mix the dry ingredients: Stir the baking powder and salt through the flour and set aside.
Cream and add the eggs: Beat the butter and sugar together, then beat in the lightly beaten eggs.
Add the lemon: Add the lemon zest and some of the lemon juice (keep a little back for the cake). Stir a couple of tablespoons of the flour in first to stop it curdling.
Fold: Fold in the rest of the flour, a little at a time if you like, then fold in the soaked oats with all their milk. Don't over-mix.

Bake: Spoon into the tin without bothering to smooth the top and bake for about 40–45 minutes, starting to check with a skewer at 40. Cover with foil if it browns too fast. It's done when the skewer comes out clean and the cake springs back.
Soak with lemon: Leave 5 minutes, lift it out, poke holes with a skewer and spoon the reserved lemon juice over so it sinks in. Let it cool.

Drizzle: Mix the icing sugar with lemon juice (and a splash of water if needed) and drizzle over the cooled cake so it runs down the sides. Add a little lemon zest on top if you like, then let it set.

recipes.title: FORGOTTEN Fairy Cakes That’ll Fly Off the Plate (Literally!) Just Like Gran Used to Make!
ingredients: All measurements in tsp, tbsp, g, ml, UK/US cups.
1–2 tbsp (15–30 ml ) milk, to loosen batter
150 ml (5 fl oz / 10 tbsp) double cream or whipping cream
Heat oven to 180°C (160°C fan) / 350°F. Line a 12-hole bun or fairy cake tin with paper cases.

Fill and bake: Put a tablespoon of batter in each case and go back around if you have mix left. Bake 15–18 minutes until golden and springy (that's from the description; the captions don't give a clear minute count). Cool.
Cut the wings: Slice a lid off each bun and cut that lid in two to make the butterfly wings.

Jam and cream: The host loosens a thick raspberry jam with a little boiling water so it can soak into the cake. Jam is not listed in the description, and no amount is given — use only as much as you see in the video, or leave it out. Whip the cream with a little icing sugar and vanilla.

recipes.title: Powdered Perfection: The Ultimate PANTRY YORKSHIRE Puddings No Fridge No Problem!
ingredients: Oil, lard, or beef dripping — 1 tsp per muffin hole (12 tsp total)
8 tbsp egg powder + 240 ml water = 4 eggs
8 tbsp milk powder + 360 ml water = 1½ cups milk
Beat until smooth. Rest 30–60 minutes at room temperature.
steps: Rehydrate the egg: Stir the egg powder into the warm water and leave for 5 minutes to thicken.
Rehydrate the milk: Mix the full-fat milk powder with its water.
Make the batter: Put the flour and salt in a bowl, add the egg mixture and milk and whisk together. A few small bits of flour are fine.
Rest: Leave the batter for 30–60 minutes (45 minutes worked best), then pour it into a jug. Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F).
Heat the fat: Put about a teaspoon of oil, lard or dripping in each hole of a muffin tin and heat it in the oven for a couple of minutes.

Bake: Pour the batter into the hot fat and bake for about 25 minutes without opening the door, until puffed and crisp. Deeper muffin tins hold the shape better than very small tins, and a larger tin makes one big pudding.
Serve: Serve with onion gravy. The same batter works for toad in the hole.

recipes.title: This Pork Schnitzel Has German Grandma Screaming "Perfekt!"
ingredients: 4 boneless pork chops (about 150–180g / 5–6 oz each)I used loin
For the Sweet & Tangy Braised Red Cabbage:
500g (½ head / about 5 cups shredded) red cabbage
¼ tsp (1.25g) ground allspice or cinnamon (optional)
steps: Braised red cabbage first: It takes about 25 minutes, so start it ahead. In a little butter over a steady flame, cook the thinly sliced onion, then add the shredded red cabbage, the peeled grated apple, about a tablespoon of brown sugar, a couple of tablespoons of apple cider vinegar (the description lists 1 tbsp vinegar and 1 tbsp sugar), salt, pepper, optional allspice or cinnamon, and the water (60 ml in the description). Put a lid on and braise about 25 minutes, stirring now and then so the liquid doesn't cook out and the cabbage doesn't catch.

Prep the schnitzel: Slice boneless pork chops or loin about a good half-inch thick and pound them out to open them up. This is the only time you really season the meat — salt and pepper (and paprika is listed) on the pork itself, not just in the flour.

Bread: Coat in flour, beaten egg, then breadcrumbs (optional grated Parmesan in the crumbs for a cheese crust; the host skipped it this time). Press the crumbs on firmly and let the breaded cutlets sit on a rack about 5 or 6 minutes so the coating sets.
Fry: Heat the oil — not so high that the crumbs burn before the pork cooks, but high enough to go golden. Fry the schnitzels in batches if they're large, until cooked through and crisp.

Dijon gravy: In the pan, melt a couple of tablespoons of butter, cook a couple of tablespoons of flour in it, then add the chicken broth and cream. Stir in Dijon mustard — the host uses three tablespoons; the description lists 2 tbsp — and a splash of Worcestershire sauce. Warm the cream through and serve the schnitzel with the gravy, the cabbage, and mash or buttered potatoes.

recipes.title: Lemon Shortbread Crumble Bars – Easy, Tangy, Irresistible!
ingredients: 1 cup / 225g unsalted butter, cold and cubed
¼ cup / 4 tbsp / 60ml fresh lemon juice
steps: Prepare: Preheat the oven to about 175–180°C and line an 8×8-inch tin (the host uses 9×7). Zest and juice the lemons.
Make the shortbread crumb: Mix the flour, powdered sugar, about a tablespoon of lemon zest and the salt. Rub or cut in the cold butter (or pulse in a food processor) into large breadcrumbs.

Bake the base: Press about two-thirds of the crumb into the tin and level it with a spoon; no need to prick it. Bake about 12–14 minutes, until golden at the edges and still pale in the middle. Let it cool a little.
Make the filling: Whisk the condensed milk with the two egg yolks, lemon juice and lemon zest until smooth and silky.

Top: Pour the filling over the base, then crumble the remaining third of the crumb gently over the top. It doesn't need to be fully covered; the host rubs together a little extra butter and flour for more topping.
Bake: Bake until the topping is golden and the centre barely jiggles (20–25 minutes in the description).
Cool and chill: Cool completely, then chill in the fridge before cutting into bars. They're sticky, like shortbread with lemon curd.

recipes.title: The Ultimate Zinger Cheese Burger: Double-Dipped & Fried
ingredients: 4 boneless chicken thighs or breasts, flattened
250 ml | 1 cup buttermilk (or milk + 1 tbsp vinegar)
2 tbsp Zinger seasoning powder (from earlier recipe)
cheese slices optional if you want to go cheeseburger
Shredded iceberg lettuce — I used curly green stuff
steps: Marinate: Soak the skinned, boned chicken thighs in buttermilk with 1 tablespoon of hot sauce (6 hours here). To make buttermilk, stir 1 tablespoon of apple cider vinegar into 1 cup of milk and leave 5 minutes.
Make the Zinger mayo: Mix about 3 tablespoons of mayo (or more) with a little sriracha, paprika and garlic powder, and chill.
First dredge: Mix a couple of tablespoons of Zinger seasoning into the flour. Lift the chicken straight from the buttermilk into the flour without draining and coat it.
Double dip: Dip each floured piece in a bowl of cold water, then back into the flour to get a gnarly coating. Rest on a rack for 10 minutes.

Fry: Semi-deep fry in oil that isn't too hot, nudging so it doesn't stick and turning it over, for a few minutes until cooked through and crisp. Rest it and sprinkle with a little more Zinger seasoning.
Build: Spread mayo on the bottom bun, add lettuce, the chicken, a cheese slice if you're making a cheeseburger, another good blob of sauce and the top bun.

recipes.title: This Will Make Your Toast Tipsy! Banana Rum Jam
ingredients: Water-bath processed (10 mins): Store in pantry for up to 1 year
steps: Mix the pectin: Stir the pectin into a couple of tablespoons of the sugar so it doesn't clump.
Mash the bananas: Peel the ripe bananas, run a knife through them and mash them in a bowl with a fork.

Dissolve the sugar: Put the mashed banana in a pan over a medium heat with the lime zest (and the lime juice from the ingredient list), the remaining sugar, the pectin-sugar mix, a little cinnamon and a pinch of salt. Cook for about 5 minutes, stirring so nothing catches, until the sugar dissolves.

ingredients: 1 tbsp / 15 ml olive oil or butter
500 g / 1.1 lb boneless chicken breast or thighs, cubed

250 g / 9 oz short pasta (fusilli, penne, or shells)

recipes.title: BUTTER Prawns  LEMON Chilli Sauce - NANDO’s Style
ingredients: Fresh red chilies — 4 to 8 (adjust to taste)
Smoked paprika — 1 tsp | 2.5 g (optional, for depth)
Xanthan gum — ¼ tsp (or omit for thinner sauce)
Optional, to make it shelf-stable (for 500 ml): sodium benzoate — 0.5 g (just under ⅛ tsp, measured accurately); ascorbic acid — ⅛ tsp (optional, keeps the colour fresh)
For the prawns (the description gives no amounts for these; spoken amounts are noted):
Black pepper (cayenne or chilli flakes optional)
Lemon chilli sauce (above) — a couple of tbsp
Green onion tops (or parsley/coriander), lemon wedges and crusty bread, to serve
steps: Make the onion and garlic purée: Blend the chopped onion and garlic with a pinch of salt, a little water (just enough for the blades to turn) and some of the olive oil until smooth.
Chop the chillies: Deseed the chillies to avoid the seeds (or for less heat) and mince them finely. The host adds a green one for colour. Be careful with your eyes and hands.

Simmer the sauce: In a small pan, combine the water, the purée, the lemon zest and juice, the vinegar, salt, sugar (the host uses dextrose) and the rest of the oil. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 5 minutes, stirring so nothing sticks.
Add the heat: Stir in the chopped chilli, smoked paprika (or a little cayenne, optional) and dried parsley, and simmer about 5 minutes more. Add the sodium benzoate now if you want it shelf-stable.

Blend and bottle: Let it cool a minute, then blend it while still hot with ¼ teaspoon of xanthan gum to thicken. Pour into bottles sterilised with boiling water. Without the preservative it keeps about 3 weeks in the fridge. Don't store it at room temperature.

Cook the prawns: Gently melt a splash of olive oil and at least 2 tablespoons of butter. Add the sliced garlic and cook about 30 seconds on a very low flame just to infuse the butter, without browning. Add the prawns, season with pepper, and cook about a minute a side until pink.

Sauce and serve: Stir in a couple of tablespoons of the lemon chilli sauce, turn off the heat and add a squeeze of lemon. Garnish with green onion tops and lemon, and serve with crusty bread for dipping.

recipes.title: Braised Cabbage & Minced Beef Soup - Gastropub Style
ingredients: Green cabbage: ½ head (400g) | cut into 2–3 wedges, core intact
Beef stock: 1.5 litres | 1500ml I used 2 oxo cubes
Caraway seeds: 1 tsp | 2g (toasted in the oil)
Sour cream: 150ml or a spoon per portion
Crusty bread or rye bread slices
steps: Cut the cabbage: Cut the cabbage into wedges, keeping the core in so they hold together. Set aside.

Prep the veg: Dice the onion. Scrub and slice the carrots, leaving the skin on. Mince the garlic. Peel the potatoes and cut them into thick slices so they don't turn to mush. Make up the beef stock (the host uses two stock cubes).

Brown the beef: Heat olive oil in a large pan, add the minced beef and season it with salt and pepper. Cook it, turning, leaving some chunks rather than breaking it all up. Colour is a bonus but not essential.

Bloom the seasonings: Add the carrots, onion and garlic and cook together about 5–6 minutes. Add the caraway seeds so they bloom in the oil, then the dried thyme and paprika (optional; smoked or sweet).
Build the soup: Add the potatoes and the tinned tomatoes, chopping whole tomatoes in the pan. Pour in some of the beef stock with the bay leaf.

Braise the cabbage: Nestle the cabbage wedges into the pan, add the rest of the stock and bring to a simmer. Cover and simmer about 30–40 minutes, until a fork goes easily into the potatoes. The cabbage can keep a little bite.

recipes.title: Creamy Chicken and Lentil Coconut Curry – One Pot Wonder!
ingredients: 1 tbsp / 15 ml oil (vegetable or coconut oil)
500 g / 1.1 lb boneless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into bite-size pieces
1 can (400 ml / 1.6 UK cup / 1.7 US cup) coconut milk
1 tin whole plum tomatoes (or chopped tomatoes), not tomato purée
Salt to taste (start with 1 tsp / 5 g)
1 tbsp / 6 g curry powder (mild or hot)
½ tsp / 1.25 g smoked paprika or chilli powder
½ tsp / 1.25 g garam masala (for finish)
steps: Oil: Put a blob of oil in a pan (ghee or whatever you have also works). Heat gently, not screaming hot.
Onions: Add the chopped onion and a little tad of salt to draw out moisture. Soften with a nice sizzle.
Garlic and ginger: Add garlic-ginger paste (or the grated ginger and minced garlic). Cook briefly to take the rawness out.
Bloom the spices: Add the spice bundle. Keep the flame down so the spices bloom and release their oils without burning.
Chicken: Tip in the bite-size chicken pieces and cook them in the spices. The pan will be fairly dry at this stage.
First coconut milk: Add a little of the coconut milk and cook gently so it blooms with the spices and chicken and the oils come out. No need to rush.
Green chilli: Add some sliced green chilli for colour.

Tomatoes: Pour in the juice from a tin of tomatoes first. Prefer whole plum tomatoes: snip them up in the tin with scissors, then stir them in. Do not use tomato purée; keep the tomato flavour mild, not overpowering. Chopped tomatoes also work.
Rest of the sauce: Stir in the rest of the coconut milk, the chicken stock, and the rinsed red lentils. It will look like a lot of liquid; the lentils absorb a lot of it.
Simmer covered: Bring up to a simmer, put a lid on, and cook for about 25 minutes. Stir several times during that 25 minutes so the lentils do not sink and stick on the bottom.
Finish uncovered: Take the lid off and give it about 5 minutes more. It stays a fairly loose, saucy curry; you could reduce it further if you want.
Coriander and garam masala: Stir in some chopped coriander (save a little for the top). Dust over a little garam masala and stir it in.
Serve: With naan, roti, rice, or bread and butter. The chicken should be tender in little bite-size pieces; the lentils soft with a tiny bit of texture. Turn the spice up or down to taste.

recipes.title: Why Are These Cod Fishcakes So Addictive?

Mix: Flake the cooled fish into the cooled mash, then add the chopped parsley and stir gently so there are still flakes of fish. Stir in about a tablespoon of cornflour (optional, to help with moisture) and a heaped teaspoon of Dijon. Season with salt and pepper if you like.

Coat: Dust them in flour (per the description), dip in beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs.
Shallow-fry: Heat a little oil in a pan and fry the fishcakes, turning a couple of times, until golden and crunchy all over and hot all the way through. Drain briefly on kitchen towel.

recipes.title: Diplomat Cream - Crème Diplomate
ingredients: Gelatin — 1 tsp (3 g) + 2 tbsp cold water
Heavy cream — 200–250 ml | ¾ to 1 cup
steps: Yolks and sugar: Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar for a couple of minutes to dissolve it (it doesn't need to be light and frothy), then gently whisk in the cornstarch.
Bloom the gelatin: Sprinkle the gelatin over the cold water and set aside.

Warm the milk: Over a gentle flame, warm the milk with the whey powder (the stabilising secret ingredient), a pinch of salt (optional) and about 2 teaspoons of vanilla, stirring to dissolve, until it steams with a bubble or two.
Temper and thicken: Stir a little of the hot milk into the yolks, then a little more, then tip it all back into the pan. Stir over a very low heat until it thickens, then take it off the flame.
Finish the pastry cream: Stir in the butter and the gelatin until smooth. Pour into a dish, press cling film onto the surface, cool, then chill for about 2 hours.
Whip the cream: Whip the heavy cream with about 1 teaspoon of icing sugar and about ½ teaspoon of vanilla.
Combine: Fold or whisk the chilled pastry cream into the whipped cream, about half at a time, until fully combined.
Use: Pipe into choux buns, eclairs or profiteroles, or use in trifles. It's stable in warm weather and keeps a couple of days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Easy Choux Pastry - Perfect for Filling!
ingredients: Unsalted butter — 60 g | ¼ cup (UK) | 4 tbsp

steps: Boil: Put the water, salt and butter in a pan and bring to the boil so the butter melts. Heat the oven to about 200°C (400°F).
Cook in the flour: Turn the heat down low (or off), add all the flour and stir until there are no lumps and it forms a smooth paste. It is very hot.
Cool slightly: Spread the paste out in the pan to cool a little; keep it warm and pliable, not cold.
Beat in the eggs: Beat in the eggs one at a time by hand. It looks runny and lumpy at first, then absorbs each egg. Keep going until you have a smooth, pipeable paste.
Pipe: Spoon it into a piping bag, cut a decent-sized opening, and pipe blobs onto a lined tray, leaving room to spread. Pat down any peaks with a wet finger so they don't burn.
Bake: Bake for about 20–25 minutes until puffed and golden.
Release the steam: Prick each puff to let the steam out, turn them over, return them to the oven with the door ajar and leave for about 10 minutes to dry.
Cool and fill: Cool completely on a rack, then fill with pastry cream, whipped cream, chocolate cream or jam and cream, and dip in chocolate if you like.

recipes.title: Processed PARMESAN Cheese Creamy, sliceable,  MELTS beautifully TOO!
ingredients: 200g (2 cups) Parmesan powder (or finely grated Parmesan)
30g (6 tsp) soy lecithin powder (or 12 tsp liquid lecithin)
2g baking soda (½ teaspoon) — optional, helps smooth but can be left out
30g (6 tsp) cornstarch or sodium citrate (for smooth emulsification)
2½ tbsp powdered gelatin (or agar-agar for a vegetarian option) (helps firm up)
a pinch of turmeric or paprika (optional, for colour)
Put in the fridge to set up for about 6 hours - leave overnight for best results.
Shelf life: 7–10 days safely in the fridge. Vacuum-sealed? You might get up to 2–3 weeks.
Cut into usable blocks or slices, wrap tightly, and freeze.
Shelf life in the freezer: Up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge overnight. Texture may soften slightly but still melts well.
steps: Grate the Parmesan: Finely grate the Parmesan, rind and all, by hand or in a food processor (or use Parmesan powder).
Warm the base: On a fairly low flame, warm the milk with the butter (melted) and whisk in the soy lecithin powder to help it emulsify. A few lumps are fine because it gets blended later.

Add the cheese and the rest: Stir in the Parmesan, then the salt, gelatin, cornflour (or sodium citrate) and baking soda (optional). Add turmeric a little at a time until you get the colour you want, or leave it out to keep the cheese white.
Thicken: Keep stirring over low heat until it thickens and turns smooth. It firms up a lot in the fridge.
Blend: Blitz it with a stick blender until completely smooth, with no flecks of powder.

Mould and set: Pour it into a mould (the host uses a clean, cut-down milk carton), tap it to level the top and release air bubbles, let it cool, cover, and refrigerate at least 6 hours, ideally overnight.

Slice and use: Turn it out and slice. It melts well on burgers (the host melts it under a lid on Italian sausage patties) and in pasta. It keeps 7–10 days in an airtight container in the fridge, or up to 3 months frozen.

recipes.title: KETCHUP Before  KETCHUP  - BRITISH UMAMI in a Bottle
ingredients: Chestnut, button or flat-cap mushrooms, finely chopped — 500 g (1.1 lb)
Allspice berries or ground allspice — ½ tsp
Malt vinegar — 300 ml (1¼ UK cups / 1¼ US cups + 1 tbsp)
steps: Chop the mushrooms (the day before): Wipe the mushrooms and chop them quite finely. Put them in a non-reactive bowl (ceramic, glass or plastic, not metal).
Salt and leave overnight: Mix in the salt so it is all the way through — it will draw out a lot of moisture. Cover and leave on the side, not in the fridge, for 24 hours.

Into the pan: The next day there will be plenty of fluid. Put the mushrooms and all that salty mushroom water into a pan with the onion, garlic, pepper, allspice (the host uses ground; berries are traditional), cloves if using, a bay leaf, and the malt vinegar from the description.
Simmer: Mix, bring it up, and simmer about 40 minutes, partially covered, stirring now and then so nothing sticks. There will be a vinegary aroma and some evaporation.

Cool and strain: Turn it off, take out the bay leaf, and let it cool. Traditionally you would wring it in a cloth once cold. The host tried blending with a stick blender after about 10 minutes, then straining in a cloth, but then recommends not blending — it makes a paste that is harder to squeeze. Squeeze out the juice and bottle it.

Store: The host says this is a vegan, Worcestershire-style seasoning, mushroom-forward, salty and sour. Kept in the fridge it will last 3 months; it has a higher mushroom content and a shorter shelf life than commercial versions.

recipes.title: Oldest BRITISH CURRY Recipe Ever Written (1751 Revival)
ingredients: 5 chicken thighs, boneless and skinless cut into chunks
1 litre (1000ml / 4 US cups / 3½ UK cups) water
3 large onions, finely chopped (approx. 400g / 14 oz / 2 cups packed)
½ tsp ground black pepper (1g / ½ tsp)
Salt, to taste (optional) not in the recipe
steps: A 1751 curry: This follows Hannah Glasse's 1751 recipe in The Art of Cookery Made Plain and Easy — the earliest known curry recipe written in English. It will not taste like a modern curry: there is no chilli, tomato or garam masala, just turmeric, ginger and pepper. The original uses two small chickens, skinned and cut as for a fricassee, stewed in a quart of water; the host uses five boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into chunks, and 1 litre of water.
Stew the chicken: Bring the water to the boil first, then add the chicken and stew about 5 minutes. Strain off the liquor and set the chicken aside in a clean dish, as the original says.

Fry the onions and bloom the spices: Chop three large onions small and fry them in the butter until soft and golden. Mix the ground turmeric, ground ginger and black pepper, stir them into the onions and let them bloom a little.

Add the liquor and cook: Pour the reserved chicken cooking water back in. Return the chicken to the pan as well — the captions are clearer about the liquor than about the exact moment the meat goes back; watch that in the video rather than inventing it. Cook uncovered 30 minutes, stirring gently now and then so nothing catches, as some of the liquid evaporates.

Cream and lemon: Stir in the cream (double or heavy; the original says a quarter of a pint) and let it cook only a very short moment. Turn the flame completely off before you add any lemon juice, so it doesn't curdle. The recipe says the juice of two lemons; the host tasted after one because the lemons were large and stopped there. Salt is optional and is not in the original recipe.

recipes.title: Devon SPLITS   Brings the KID out in ME!
ingredients: 250 ml (8.5 fl oz / 1 UK cup / 1 US cup) double cream (or heavy whipping cream)

steps: Bloom the yeast: Stir the yeast into the warm milk and leave it about 5 minutes until it bubbles and froths. If it doesn't, add more yeast.

Make the dough: Mix 250 g bread flour and 250 g plain flour with the sugar and salt (all bread flour or all plain flour also works). First rise: With floured hands, tuck the dough into a ball and put it in a buttered bowl. Cover it (a plastic bag works) and leave until doubled in size.

Shape: Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and divide it into about eight, weighing the pieces if you like. Tuck each piece into a roll and put them on a parchment-lined tray. Cover and leave to rise again.
Bake: Bake at 190°C for about 18–22 minutes until golden. You can brush them with milk before baking; the host doesn't.
Butter: About a minute after they come out, brush the tops with melted butter for a soft, darker top (or use a sugar glaze). Leave them to cool.

Fill: Cut each bun on a diagonal from the top, without going all the way through. Spread jam generously inside on both sides so it is fully coated, then fill with plenty of cream.

ingredients: Dried chives or onion powder — 1½ tsp

recipes.title: Old Fashioned Potato & Bacon Soup
ingredients: Salt, pepper, thyme to taste (approx. 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper, 1/2 tsp dried thyme)

steps: Cook the bacon: Chop the streaky bacon (scissors are fine). Start it in a little butter or oil and render the fat until it has some colour — the host wants visible pieces, not only tiny crisp bits. Thicken and finish: If you want it thicker, stir in a cornflour slurry (the host uses a tablespoon of cornflour mixed with water — the water amount is not stated) and cook a little longer, about an extra 5 minutes. Stir in the cream or milk (1 cup in the description), then half of the bacon, saving the rest for garnish.

recipes.title: Creamy Tuscan Chicken  – Family Favourite One Tray Meal!
ingredients: ½ cup | 50 g grated Parmesan cheese
¼ tsp | 0.5 g red pepper flakes (optional)
½ cup | 60 g chopped sun-dried tomatoes, drained
1 red or yellow bell pepper, sliced
Optional: pinch of oregano or smoked paprika
steps: Prep: Season the bone-in chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Strip the spinach leaves, cut the onion, slice the courgette into thick pieces (it turns watery when cooked) and slice or dice the peppers. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).

Make the sauce: Over a gentle heat, cook a heaped tablespoon of tomato paste with a little butter to take out its sourness. Stir in the smoked paprika and chilli flakes to bloom, then add the stock, at least a cup of cream and the Parmesan.
Add the spinach: As soon as the sauce starts to bubble, stir in the spinach to wilt, then turn off the flame.

recipes.title: NOT Just EGG - SMOOTH Pourable SCRAMBLES like a real egg!
ingredients: Split mung beans, soaked overnight — 300 g
Fresh water — 720 ml | 3 UK cups | 3 US cups
Canola oil (or avocado/neutral) — 90 ml | 6 tbsp | ¼ UK cup + 2 tbsp
Psyllium husk powder — 1.5 g | ½ tsp
steps: Soak the mung beans: Leave the split mung beans in water overnight, then rinse them three or four times until the yellow water runs clear.

Blend everything: Put the fresh water in a blender, then add the drained mung beans, cornstarch, turmeric, nutritional yeast, garlic powder, baking powder, onion powder, canola oil, psyllium husk, the black salt (the only salt used) and about a tablespoon of carrot juice for colour. Blend until completely smooth.
Rest: Leave the mixture for about 20 minutes so the cornstarch and psyllium husk can thicken it.

Scramble: Warm a small pan as you would for eggs, pour in about two ladles of the mix and turn the heat down so it sets. Leave it to set like an omelette at first, then move it about gently, letting it set a little before turning so it doesn't turn stodgy. Cook on low until it comes together like scrambled egg, browning it lightly if you like, and serve on toast.

Omelette: Heat a little butter or oil in the pan and add about one and a half ladles. Cook low and slow like a flatbread until it releases from the pan and the top sets and turns matte (a lid would speed this up). Brown the underside, turn it, colour the other side and fold. Filling it with cheese and tomato before folding while it is still too soft makes it break up, so let it set first.

recipes.title: TRADITIONAL  Yorkshire Pikelets – Old Fashioned GRIDDLE CRUMPETS
ingredients: 250 g (1½ UK cups / 2 US cups) strong white bread flour – All-purpose/plain flour works

recipes.title: COSORI TwinFry Air Fryer - Chicken and Broccoli ALFREDO Stuffed JACKET Potatoes
ingredients: 2-4 large baking potatoes (about 250g / 9 oz each) I used 2 @ 400g each
1 cup (240 ml / 240 g / 8.5 oz) whole milk (UK: 250 ml / g)
½ cup (120 ml / 120 g / 4.2 oz) double/heavy cream
½ cup (40 g / 1.4 oz) grated Parmesan cheese
1 cup (150 g / 5.3 oz) cooked chicken, shredded or diced
1 cup (90 g / 3.2 oz) cooked broccoli, finely chopped
¼ tsp (1.25 ml / 1.25 g) salt (adjust to taste)
¼ tsp (1.25 ml / 1.25 g) black pepper
¼ tsp (1.25 ml / 1.25 g) garlic powder (optional)
½ cup (50 g / 1.8 oz) grated mozzarella or cheddar cheese
Preheat your Cosori air fryer to 200°C (390°F).
Cook for 40–45 minutes, no foil, until crisp outside and soft inside. (Flip after 25 mins if desired.
Return stuffed potatoes to the air fryer at 190°C (380°F) for 5–8 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and golden.
steps: Cook the jackets: Prick 2–4 large baking potatoes all over, rub with olive oil and a pinch of salt, and cook them without foil until the skins are crisp and the insides are soft. In an air fryer, preheat to 200°C (390°F) and cook 40–45 minutes, flipping after 25 minutes if you like. The host notes this is roughly half the oven time; you can bake them in a regular oven instead — watch the video rather than inventing an oven time. For a softer skin, wrap the cooked potatoes in foil for about 5 minutes after they come out.

Alfredo sauce: Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook the rawness out, then add the milk, stirring so there are no lumps, and the cream. Season with black pepper and optional garlic powder — the host skips extra salt at this stage because of the Parmesan. Stir in the grated Parmesan until you have a thick sauce.
Filling: Stir the cooked shredded or diced chicken and the cooked, finely chopped broccoli into the sauce and let the chicken warm through.
Stuff: Cut the potatoes, scoop some of the flesh out and stir it into the Alfredo, then pack the filling back into the shells. Top with grated mozzarella or cheddar if you like.

Finish: Return the stuffed potatoes to the air fryer at 190°C (380°F) for 5–8 minutes (or the oven) until the cheese is bubbly and golden. Use a tray if you don't want cheese dripping into the basket.

recipes.title: Yorkshire Teacakes – Soft, Fruity & Made for Butter
ingredients: 250 g bread flour 250 g All-purpose/plain flour (3¼ UK cups / 4 US cups)
1 tsp (2.5 g) ground mixed spice (or use ½ tsp cinnamon + ½ tsp allspice)
100 g mixed dried fruit (raisins, currants, sultanas)
Optional: extra flour for shaping and 1 tbsp milk for brushing
steps: Bloom the yeast: Stir the yeast into the warm milk and leave it a couple of minutes until it starts to froth.

Mix the dough: In a stand mixer bowl (or by hand), combine 250 g plain flour and 250 g bread flour with the salt, sugar, dried fruit and mixed spice, and stir the dry ingredients together. Add the yeasted milk, egg and melted butter and knead with the dough hook into a dough that is slightly sticky but not wet.
First rise: With lightly floured hands, fold the dough over, put it in a lightly buttered bowl and cover it (a plastic bag works) until doubled in size, about 1 hour to 1 hour 10 minutes.
Shape: Knock the dough back and divide it into about eight pieces, weighing them if you like. Shape each into a ball and put them on a lined tray. It doesn't matter if they end up touching.
Second rise: Cover again and leave for about 40 minutes. You can brush them with milk at this point; the host doesn't.
Bake: Bake at 190°C for up to about 15 minutes, until golden. The description gives 18–22 minutes, until golden on top and hollow-sounding underneath.

Butter and cool: Straight from the oven, brush the tops with melted butter for a soft sheen (or use a sugar glaze if you prefer). Leave them 5 minutes, then cool on a rack. Serve split and toasted with butter or raspberry jam.

recipes.title: GREEK-Style LEMON Chicken Thighs with Roast Potatoes
ingredients: 2 tbsp (30 ml) fresh lemon juice (about ½ lemon)
1 tbsp (15 g) Dijon mustard (optional, adds depth)
½ tsp (0.5 g) dried thyme or rosemary
4–6 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 1.2 kg / 2.5 lb)
Salt & pepper to season the skin
750 g (1.6 lb) potatoes (e.g. Maris Piper or Yukon Gold)
Drizzle of olive oil for roasting
½ tsp dried thyme or a few sprigs fresh
Optional: ½ tsp (2.5 ml) honey or a squeeze of lemon
Optional: 1 tsp (3 g) cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp (15 ml) cold water
Optional: small knob of butter or extra lemon juice to finish
steps: Parboil the potatoes: Peel and cube the potatoes, put them in cold salted water, bring to the boil and boil 8 minutes. Drain, return them to the hot pan for a moment to dry, and shake them to rough up the edges.

Make the marinade: Mix the minced garlic, lemon zest and juice, about a tablespoon of red wine vinegar, the Dijon, olive oil, oregano, thyme, salt and pepper. Add a little sugar if it's too sour for you.

Marinate the chicken: Pat the thighs dry, loosen the skin and rub a little marinade underneath and on the underside, keeping the skin dry so it crisps. Season the skin with salt and pepper and leave about 30 minutes. Keep the rest of the marinade for the sauce.
Season the carrots: Toss the baby carrots with olive oil, a pinch of salt and thyme.

Roast: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Put a little oil in a roasting tray, spread the potatoes over it (with any leftover garlic trimmings), and sit the chicken on top so its juices baste the potatoes. Roast about 20 minutes.
Add the carrots: Tuck the carrots in around the edges and roast about 35 minutes more, until the chicken is cooked through.

Make the lemon sauce: Mix the remaining marinade with the chicken stock, bring it to the boil in a pan and simmer about a minute. Thicken lightly with the cornflour slurry (loosen with more stock if it gets too thick), then finish with a knob of butter. Add a little sugar if it's too sour.

Finish the potatoes: Lift out the chicken, stir the potatoes and carrots and roast about 8 minutes more to colour them (adding lemon wedges if you like). Cover the chicken loosely with foil meanwhile.
Serve: Plate the potatoes, carrots and chicken and spoon over the lemon sauce.

recipes.title: Easy Bacon Floodies – Old School Northern British Comfort Food
ingredients: Mashed potato (plain, not buttery) — 250 g | 9 oz
Salt — ½ tsp (less if your mash is salted)
Milk — 60 ml | 2 fl oz | ¼ UK/US cup | 4 tbsp (add more if needed)
Cooked streaky bacon, chopped — 120 g | 4 oz
Butter, lard, or oil — for frying
steps: Two versions: The host makes bacon floodies two ways: with plain mashed potato (no butter or milk in the mash — leftovers are fine) and with raw grated potato. For the grated version, salt the potato, leave it about 5 minutes, then wring it out well. The description lists 250 g mashed potato for 8–10 floodies.

Make a stodgy batter: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt (less if the mash is already salted) and black pepper with the egg and the milk (60 ml in the description, plus more if you want it thinner). Some people throw everything in together; the host makes the batter first and then folds in the potato and the chopped cooked streaky bacon (120 g in the description).

Fry the bacon fat if you need it: The host cooks the bacon first, chops it with scissors, and likes to fry the floodies in a little of that fat. Butter, lard or oil also work. You don't really need extra oil if you have bacon fat.

Cook low and slow: Spoon the mix into the pan — you can use a ring if you want a tidy shape. Fry on a low heat about 3–5 minutes, then turn (and turn again if you need to) so the flour and potato cook all the way through. Don't rush them.
Serve: They're good with brown sauce or ketchup, or topped with a fried egg, or with cheese melted under the grill. You can also reheat them in the microwave.

recipes.title: CARROT Cake Cookies - The ONLY WAY to Eat Carrot Cake Without a Fork!
ingredients: 4 tbsp (60ml) melted coconut oil or neutral oil
Optional: 2 tbsp (16g) extra almond flour if dough feels sticky
225g (8 oz) full-fat cream cheese (cold but soft enough to beat)
Optional: 1 tbsp milk powder or 1 tsp cornstarch for added firmness
steps: Mix the dry ingredients: In a bowl, stir together the rolled oats, raisins, walnuts, the raising agent (the host says baking powder; the description lists baking soda), salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, almond flour and grated carrot until evenly mixed, so the carrot doesn't clump.

Add the wet ingredients: Add a couple of teaspoons of vanilla, the coconut oil and the weighed maple syrup, and stir well. There's no egg; the carrots release moisture as they bake. If you can't get maple syrup, use honey with 1 tsp of molasses or black treacle stirred in.

Rest: Leave the mix about 15 minutes so the oats absorb the moisture. Only then, if it is still too wet, add a couple of tablespoons of almond flour; if it is too dry, add a tablespoon or two of milk or water.

Make the filling: Squash the cold cream cheese and butter together with a spatula, then beat in the powdered sugar and vanilla until smooth. A tablespoon of milk powder or about a teaspoon of cornflour will firm it up. Cover and chill so it stays firm.
Shape: Preheat the oven to about 175°C and line a tray with parchment. Roll the dough into balls of about 30–32 g, space them out on the tray and flatten them slightly.
Bake: Bake about 12–15 minutes, until the tops are a little crisp but the middles are still soft. Leave them on the tray a minute, then cool completely on a rack.
Sandwich and set: Spread or pipe the cream cheese filling onto half the cookies and top with the rest. Chill in a box for about an hour so the filling sets.

recipes.title: Cauliflower Steak Bake with Spinach Ricotta and Marinara Sauce — This really Stacks up!
ingredients: 1 large head cauliflower, cut into 5–6 thick steaks (¾–1 inch)
1 cup cooked spinach, drained and finely chopped
1½ cups | 360 ml 1½ US cups | 1⅓ UK cups passata
1 tsp | 5 ml dried oregano or basil if no Italain herbs
Pinch of sugar to balance the acidity
½ tsp dried oregano or Italian seasoning
steps: Heat the oven: Put it on about 220°C to start; it will be turned down to 180°C later.

Roast the cauliflower: Cut a large head into thick steaks (the description says 5–6 steaks, ¾–1 inch) and keep the leftover bits for the layers. Rub with a little olive oil, salt and pepper, and bake about 25 minutes (the description says 25–30 minutes, flipping halfway). It only needs to take some colour; it will go into the bake.

Blanch the spinach: Wash and roughly chop the spinach. In a pan with a lid, blanch it in a little boiling water from the kettle for about a minute, no longer (or steam it if you prefer). Drain and let it cool, then chop again if you want.
Make a quick marinara: Cook a couple of cloves of garlic in a little olive oil, then add the passata with Italian herbs (or oregano or basil), salt, pepper and a little sugar to taste.

Spinach-ricotta and crumb: Stir the cooled spinach through the ricotta and add a little nutmeg. For the topping, mix breadcrumbs (panko in the description) with Parmesan (from the description), oregano or Italian seasoning, and garlic powder if you are using it. The host also mentions maybe a little mozzarella over the top, which is not listed in the description — use it only if you want, and don't invent an amount.

Layer in an 8 × 8 × 2 inch dish: Turn the oven down to 180°C. Sauce in the bottom, then cauliflower, then spinach-ricotta (the host aims for about two layers of that), more marinara, more cauliflower. Finish with the Parmesan breadcrumb topping and a little mozzarella if using. The dish may bubble over, so stand it on a tray.

Bake: Cover with foil (oiled if you wish) for about 15 minutes, then take the foil off and bake about another 20 minutes until bubbling and golden on top. Let it cool about 10 minutes before slicing, like a lasagna.

recipes.title: Strawberry Banana BREAD – A Fruity Twist on a Classic Favourite
ingredients: 115g (½ cup) unsalted butter, melted (or vegetable oil)
150g (¾ cup) granulated sugar or brown sugar
1 tbsp all-purpose flour (for coating strawberries, prevents sinking)
Extra sliced strawberries for the top
1 tbsp coarse sugar for a crunchy topping
steps: Mash the bananas: Mash the ripe bananas with a fork or beater and leave them a while. Left an hour or more they darken, which gives a darker loaf; the host leaves them about 10 minutes.
Prepare: Preheat the oven to about 175–180°C and line a 2 lb (9×5-inch) loaf tin.
Beat the eggs and sugar: Beat the eggs with the sugar until creamy and frothy. Mix in the vanilla, yogurt (or buttermilk), melted butter and mashed banana.
Coat the strawberries: Toss the diced strawberries with a tablespoon of flour so they don't sink.
Combine: Mix the flour with the salt, baking soda, baking powder and cinnamon, then stir it into the wet mixture until combined. Fold in the strawberries.
Fill and decorate: Pour the batter into the middle of the tin (smoothing it is optional) and arrange sliced strawberries on top, with coarse sugar if you like.
Bake: Bake about 50–60 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Leave 10 minutes in the tin, then cool completely on a rack before slicing. Serve with butter.

recipes.title: How To Make PERFECT Pulled BEEF every time! Foolproof!
ingredients: Beef chuck or brisket — 1 kg | 2.2 lbs | about 4 UK cups | 4¼ US cups (cut into large chunks)
Black pepper — ½ tsp | 2.5 g | 2.5 ml
Beef stock or broth — 250 ml | 250 g | 1 UK cup | 1.06 US cups
Optional: Worcestershire sauce — 1 tbsp | 15 ml | 15 g for extra depth
Natural release for 10–15 minutes, then quick release any remaining pressure.
steps: Season and sear: Season the beef (any cut; chuck or brisket in large chunks) with salt and pepper. Sear it all over in hot oil, just for colour, not to cook it through, then set it aside on a tray.
Onions and garlic: Without cleaning the pan, add a touch more oil and cook the onion and garlic briefly, scraping up the bits from the bottom. Add some pepper.

Build the gravy: Stir in about 2 tablespoons of Worcestershire sauce (or soy sauce) and about 2 tablespoons of tomato paste, and cook briefly to remove the tomato's sourness. Stir in the beef stock or gravy (gravy powder, granules or stock cubes all work) to deglaze the pan.

Pressure cook: Pour the onion gravy into the Instant Pot liner, add the beef and its juices (it doesn't need to be submerged) and pressure cook on normal/high for 60 minutes. Let it release naturally for about 10–15 minutes, then release the rest. Without an Instant Pot, simmer on the stove for about 3 hours until it falls apart.
Pull: Lift the beef out and shred it with two forks, as fine or chunky as you like. Mix in a little of the cooking liquid to keep it moist.

Gravy and storage: Thicken the leftover liquid in a pan with a little cornflour for gravy. The beef freezes well in some of its gravy; reheat in the microwave for about a minute and serve in crusty bread.

recipes.title: Ultimate Chicken Cordon Bleu Rolls – Crispy, Juicy & Garlic Loaded!
ingredients: 2–4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts, depending on size
Salt and black pepper, to taste
½ tsp paprika (optional, for extra colour)
steps: Make the filling: Mix the softened cream cheese and softened unsalted butter with the minced garlic, chopped parsley, optional onion powder, salt and a little pepper. If you use salted butter, skip the added salt.

Prep the chicken: Butterfly 2–4 boneless chicken breasts, depending on size, and pound them out so they will roll. Season with a little salt and pepper — the host seasons one side before pounding, not both sides.

Fill, roll and freeze: Spread some of the garlic filling on the chicken, add a slice of packet ham, and roll it up. No toothpicks — wrap it tightly in cling film, twisting both ends, and freeze until solid so it holds its shape for breading.

Bread: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Set up flour, beaten eggs mixed with a couple of tablespoons of cornflour (the mixture needs to be sticky because the frozen rolls will start to give off moisture), and breadcrumbs seasoned with a little salt and paprika (the host doesn't usually season breadcrumbs, but does here because the chicken is already frozen). Coat flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.

Fry and bake: Heat the oil and shallow-fry the rolls just until you have a golden coating — the host talks about about a minute, turning them around — then transfer to a tray and bake about 25 minutes, or until the middle reaches 75°C (165°F).

recipes.title: Sweet and Sour Paneer Takeaway Style
ingredients: Self-raising flour — 100g / ¾ cup (UK & US) / 7 tbsp

steps: Make the sauce: Stir together the ketchup, light soy sauce, a couple of tablespoons of sugar, about 2 tablespoons of white vinegar, optional pineapple juice from the tin, and the water (4 tbsp in the description). Batter the paneer: Mix the self-raising flour, cornflour, salt and white pepper, then add water (about 100 ml, adjusted) until you have a thick coating batter. Cube the paneer (250 g) and coat it.

Vegetables and finish: In a pan, cook the chunked onion and red and green peppers just enough to take the rawness off — keep some crunch. Add optional pineapple chunks. Pour in the sauce, thicken with the slurry (the longer it cooks, the thicker it gets), and toss the fried paneer through so there is enough sauce to coat. Serve with fried rice or noodles.

recipes.title: Chunky, Cheesy, and 100% Real – The Ultimate Ham & Veggie Chowder / Soup – No Cans, Just Comfort!
ingredients: 30g plain flour (¼ UK cup | ¼ US cup)
120g grated cheddar cheese (1 UK cup | 1 US cup)

recipes.title: I’ll Never Buy Passata Again After This…

recipes.title: Cosori TwinFry Air Fryer - My GO TO method for PERFECT chips Every time!
ingredients: Potatoes (Maris Piper or Russet) 500g | 1.1 lb | 3 medium. (the host says any potatoes work)
Optional seasoning: garlic powder, smoked paprika, vinegar salt, etc.
steps: Cut the chips: Wash the potatoes. Peel them for regular chips, or leave the skin on for steak-fry style, and cut into chips.
Soak: Put the chips in a bowl of water with a little salt and soak at least 30 minutes (or overnight) to draw out starch.
Dry: Drain and rinse, dry them in a tea towel, then go over them with kitchen towel until fully dry so they crisp.

Season and oil: Toss with salt and a little oil of your choice. If you use cornflour (best for thinner chips), coat the dry chips evenly with about a tablespoon first, then add the oil so there are no powdery patches.

Air-fry: Pile them into the air fryer basket (the host fills the whole large basket) and cook at 200°C for about 20 minutes, taking the basket out to shake halfway. Add about 5 minutes more if a crowded basket needs it. The description suggests preheating 3 minutes, then 15–20 minutes for thinner fries or 20–25 for chunky chips.
Serve: Season to taste, with garlic powder, smoked paprika or vinegar salt if you like.
