recipes.title: CRISPY Coconut CHICKEN with Bang Bang Sauce
steps: Make the bang bang sauce: Mix the mayonnaise with the sriracha and the sweet chilli sauce, plus a little lime juice if you like (or other hot sauce), and set aside so the flavours come together.
Season the chicken: Pat the chicken tenders dry with kitchen towel and toss with about a teaspoon of smoked paprika, about a teaspoon of garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Flour: Toss the seasoned chicken in the bowl with the flour to coat. This saves setting up a separate station.
Egg and coconut crumb: Mix the panko and coconut on a tray. Dip each tender in beaten egg, then press it into the coconut crumb, using one wet hand and one dry. Chilling them helps the coating stick.

Shallow fry: Heat oil in a pan until a skewer bubbles. Fry the tenders slowly without crowding, turning often, so they crisp without browning too fast before the chicken cooks through. Air frying with an oil spray, or part-frying and finishing in the oven, also works.
Rest and serve: Rest them briefly on a rack (they keep cooking), then serve with the bang bang sauce for dipping or drizzling.

recipes.title: Strawberry PEACH Pie – A CLASSIC Made Simple
ingredients: For the Pie Crust (Homemade or Store-Bought):
(Or use a pre-made 9-inch pie crust for convenience.)
1 can (400g/14 oz) peach slices in juice, well-drained and chopped
250g (2 cups) fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced
1 tbsp unsalted butter, cubed (for dotting on top)
1 egg yolk + 1 tbsp milk (for egg wash)
steps: Mix the filling: In a bowl combine the well-drained, chopped tinned peaches, the hulled sliced strawberries, granulated and brown sugar, 2 tablespoons of cornstarch, 1 tablespoon of lemon juice, a little vanilla, and optional cinnamon. The host also adds a pinch of salt to cut the sweetness (salt is not listed in the description). Leave it about 10 minutes.
Line the dish: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Roll homemade or store-bought pastry to fit a 9-inch pie dish and come up the sides with a little overhang.

Fill and finish the top: Tip in the fruit. You can add a lid or a lattice; the host starts to talk about a lattice and then decides on an open pie. Dot the filling with small cubes of unsalted butter — don't go crazy. If you do add a lid or lattice, an egg-yolk-and-milk wash and a little coarse sugar are listed as optional.
Bake: Sit the dish on a tray and bake 45–55 minutes until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbling.

recipes.title: EASY Paneer CHEESE from Scratch
ingredients: Full-fat whole milk — 5 litres (21¼ cups UK | 21¼ cups US)
Apple cider vinegar — 7½ tbsp (110 ml | 110 g | 11 UK tsp | 15 US tsp)
(or use half vinegar, half lemon juice for a milder taste)
steps: Set up: You need a large pan, cheesecloth (cotton cloth) and, optionally, two square baskets so the paneer comes out square. The host uses 10×8×3-inch baskets; use smaller ones for less milk.

Heat the milk: Pour the milk into the pan and add the salt now if you're using it (a couple of teaspoons). Heat it, stirring now and then so it doesn't catch, and more often once it steams. Watch closely, because it goes from steaming to boiling over quickly. The description says to bring it slowly to 85–90°C.

Split the milk: When it is steaming and just starting to bubble, add the vinegar (or half vinegar, half lemon juice) and keep heating about 25 seconds so it mixes in. Turn the heat off and leave it 10 minutes to split fully into curds and whey.
Drain: Line a basket with cheesecloth and set it on a rack over a tray or in the sink. Carefully ladle in the hot curds and let the whey drain away. The host uses the whey on his plants.
Press: Level the curds, fold the cloth over, set the second basket inside, then a board and a heavy weight on top (the host uses about 6 kg). More weight and longer pressing give firmer paneer.
Turn out: After about an hour, remove the weight, turn the paneer out and cube it, trimming the edges square if you like.

recipes.title: Ultimate SHREDDED BEEF Pie
ingredients: Beef chuck, shin, or brisket — 500g | 1 lb
Refrigerated pie crusts — about 400g total | UK/US: 2 crusts, shortcrust and puff pastry
steps: Season and brown the beef: Season cheap stewing beef (chuck, shin or brisket, about 500 g) with salt and pepper — better on the meat than in flour — and cut it quite large. Brown it in a little olive oil.

Aromatics and pressure-cook: Cook the chopped onion (and minced garlic from the list) just to take the rawness out, then add the beef broth or water (250 ml), about a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce, and about a teaspoon of dried thyme. Pressure-cook on high 45 minutes, then natural release at least 10 minutes (longer is fine).

Shred and thicken: The meat should be tender enough to shred. In a pan, cook a couple of tablespoons of flour over a moderate flame to take the rawness out, then stir in the cooking liquid and let it thicken into gravy. Season to taste. Mix enough gravy through the shredded beef to keep it moist, and keep some back — you can add an extra teaspoon in the pie if it looks dry. The captions are clearer about moistening the meat than about the exact shredding moment; watch the video if you want to see how he pulls it.

Line and fill: Heat the oven — the host says about 180°C; the description says 190°C / 375°F. Roll shortcrust (ready-rolled is fine) to fit your tins with a little overhang, then trim. Fill with the beef.

Lid and bake: Roll puff pastry for the lids (or use shortcrust throughout). Brush a little beaten egg around the rim to glue them, add the lids, and bake 30–35 minutes until golden. Rest about 6 or 7 minutes before serving. It's a fairly solid meat pie.

recipes.title: Chicken Cordon Bleu Casserole  -  No Tinned Soup
ingredients: 3 cups cooked chicken, shredded or diced — 450g
2 cups shredded Swiss cheese (or mix Swiss & mozzarella) — 200g
1½ cups milk — 360ml — 360g — 1½ UK cups — 1½ US cups
1 cup chicken stock (low salt) — 240ml — 240g — 1 UK cup — 1 US cup
½ cup sour cream — 120ml — 120g — ½ UK cup — ½ US cup
1 tsp Dijon mustard — 5g (optional, adds that classic cordon bleu zing)
steps: Prep the chicken and ham: Cube (or shred) the cooked chicken, removing the skin, and cube or tear the ham, keeping the pieces big enough to see. Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and grease a 9×13 inch dish set on a tray in case it bubbles over.
Make the topping: Mix the breadcrumbs with about a teaspoon of garlic powder, pepper and a little salt (go easy if topping with Parmesan), then stir in the melted butter.

Make the sauce: Melt the butter in a pan, stir in a couple of tablespoons of flour and cook briefly. Add the milk all in one go and stir until smooth. Season with pepper (no salt) and garlic powder, and stir in the remaining sauce ingredients from the list (chicken stock, sour cream and Dijon). If it gets too thick, loosen with a little more milk or water.
Combine: Stir the chicken and ham into the sauce, then the cheese: Swiss, mozzarella (used here for stringiness), or a mix.

Top and bake: Tip into the dish and cover with the breadcrumbs, leaving little peaks. Add a little more cheese and some Parmesan and pepper, then bake for about 25–30 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Rest and serve: Rest 5–10 minutes, sprinkle with parsley and serve with broccoli, carrots or salad.

recipes.title: Easy CHICKEN Meatball Boats with Garlic Butter Hoagie Rolls
ingredients: Hoagie rolls or sub buns, about 6 in / 15 cm — 4
Cooked meatballs — 12–16 (about 360 g total, roughly 30 g each)
Marinara sauce — 360 ml (1½ cups / about 350 g)
Garlic powder — ½ tsp (or 1 clove fresh garlic, finely minced)
Dried Italian herbs or oregano — ½ tsp
steps: Heat the oven: Put it on about 190°C / 380°F — you'll cook the meatballs and later melt the cheese in the same oven. You could pan-fry the balls instead, but the oven is already on.

Mix the meatballs: Soak the breadcrumbs in a little milk or water, then mix them with the chicken mince, egg, salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, Italian herbs and optional grated Parmesan. It will still be a bit sticky, but the crumbs help you roll 12–16 balls (about 30 g each in the description). Oil the tin and your hands if it helps.

Bake the balls and crisp the rolls: Bake the meatballs 15–18 minutes, turning them after about 4 or 5 minutes. Meanwhile, mix melted butter with garlic (fresh minced, or garlic powder) and Italian herbs or oregano. Split the hoagie rolls and hollow them into boats without going right through to the bottom — or squash the insides down. Brush with the garlic butter and bake 4–5 minutes until lightly crisp. Leftover bread can go in as croutons.
Sauce and assemble: Warm the marinara. Put a little mozzarella in each boat, add the cooked meatballs (12–16, or about 360 g total), more sauce, more mozzarella and a little Parmesan.
Finish: Bake the filled boats 10–12 minutes until the cheese is bubbling. Garnish with fresh basil if you like.

recipes.title: Britain’s OLDEST seasonal bake  Simnel Cake EASTER and Mothering Sunday Cake
ingredients: Light brown sugar — 225g | 1 cup (UK & US) | 16 tbsp
Plain flour (all-purpose) — 225g | 1 ¾ cups (US) | 1 ½ cups (UK)
Milk — 2 tbsp | 30ml | 2 US tbsp | 2 UK tbsp
(Divided: ⅓ for middle layer, ⅓ for top, ⅓ for decoration)
steps: Prepare: Preheat the oven to about 150°C and line an 8-inch springform tin.

Make the batter: Cream the butter and brown sugar together (melted butter makes it easier). Beat in the four eggs; the host adds them all at once. Add part of the flour (with the baking powder and a pinch of salt), the ground almonds and spices, then the milk and the rest of the flour, and beat until smooth. Scrape down the sides.
Add the fruit: Stir in the halved cherries, lemon and orange zest, mixed peel, sultanas and currants until evenly mixed. You can mix and match the dried fruit.

Marzipan layer: Spoon about half the batter into the tin. Roll out a third of the marzipan on icing sugar or flour, cut it to the size of the tin, lay it on the batter, then cover with the rest of the batter and smooth it roughly.

Bake: Bake about 90 minutes, then test with a skewer. If it is still a little damp, cover the top with foil and give it about 20 minutes more. Cool in the tin about 10 minutes, then on a rack until completely cold. Cracks don't matter, because the top is covered.

Marzipan top: Brush the top of the cake with warmed apricot jam (optional). Roll out another third of the marzipan a little larger than the cake (a pie tin makes a handy guide), lay it over and trim it or press the edges against the sides.
Decorate and finish: Roll the remaining marzipan into 11 balls and arrange them on top. Brush everything with beaten egg yolk, then lightly toast it with a kitchen blowtorch.

recipes.title: EASY Soft CRUST FRENCH Bread
ingredients: 500g / 3¼ UK cups / 4 US cups strong white bread flour. I used 250g All-purpose/plain flour and 250g bread flour
300ml lukewarm water (about 35°C) 1¼ UK cups / 1¼ US cups
steps: Mix the dough: In a stand-mixer bowl, combine 250 g plain flour and 250 g bread flour with the yeast, sugar, salt, about a tablespoon of olive oil and the lukewarm water. Blooming the yeast in the water for 5 minutes first is optional.
Knead: Mix on low until combined, then up a notch, letting the machine knead until the dough comes away from the sides: slightly tacky but not sticky. Add a little flour or water if needed.
First rise: Shape into a ball, put it in an oiled bowl, cover and leave for an hour or more until doubled.
Shape: Dust with flour, divide the dough, and roll each piece up tightly, sealing the seam and rolling the edges, into loaves of any size.
Second rise: Place in a baguette tray, cover and leave for about 20–40 minutes until puffed up.

Score and bake: Score the tops with a knife or lame. Put a tray of boiling water in the bottom of the oven (220°C/430°F in the description) for steam, then bake for about 20–25 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding.
Cool: Leave a minute, then cool on a rack.

recipes.title: Mini Burger Steaks with Mushroom Gravy
ingredients: All-purpose/ plain flour: 2 tbsp / 16g, depending how the beef broth is made
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs: Stir the milk into the breadcrumbs and set them aside to absorb it. This keeps the burgers juicy instead of dense.
Prep the veg: Slice the mushrooms (any shape), finely chop the onion and mince the garlic.
Mix the beef: Season the mince with salt and pepper (mixed herbs are optional), add the soaked breadcrumbs and mix well by hand.
Shape: Divide the mix into about eight balls (or up to 12 for smaller ones), then flatten them into patties and press a thumb dent into the middle of each so they don't swell up as they cook.
Brown the patties: Fry in a little oil in batches, about 3–4 minutes a side, turning as often as you like, until well coloured. Transfer to a tray and cover with foil.

Make the gravy: In the same pan, melt a good couple of tablespoons of butter and cook the onion and garlic until translucent (a little colour is fine). Add the mushrooms and cook until coloured. Pour in the beef broth (the host makes it from gravy powder) and simmer gently. If your broth is thin, make a roux with the flour first.
Simmer together: Return the patties, spoon the gravy over them and simmer about 6–7 minutes, until thickened and heated through.
Mash and serve: Boil peeled, cubed potatoes in salted water until they break up, drain, and mash with salt, pepper, warm milk and butter. Serve the burger steaks and mushroom gravy over the mash.

ingredients: Breadcrumbs — ⅓ UK cup / ¼ US cup / 3 tbsp / 20 g
Garlic, minced — 1 clove (or ½ tsp garlic powder)
Beef broth, low sodium — ½ UK cup / 120 ml
Bacon rashers, chopped, or bacon bits — 3–4 (optional)

Mix the meatballs: Add the beef mince (300 g minimum in the description), the beaten egg, grated Parmesan, parsley or mixed herbs, about ½ teaspoon garlic powder (or a minced clove), oregano or a pinch of Italian herbs, salt and pepper. Mix until it is tacky and everything is incorporated, then roll into balls.
Brown them: Heat 1–2 tablespoons of oil and fry the meatballs, then take them out. They will finish in the sauce.

Sauce: Drain off some of the excess oil if there is a lot. The host treats bacon as optional; if you use it, you can crisp it first. Cook the chopped onion and garlic, and the grated carrot, then add the beef broth (120 ml in the description) and the marinara — jar or homemade — without extra salt at this stage because the sauce is already seasoned.

Simmer: Return the meatballs and cook about 20 minutes (the host also says about 25), with a lid on if you like, until they are cooked through and the sauce has thickened. Stir now and then so nothing catches.

Spaghetti and serve: Boil the spaghetti in salted water as usual. Toss some of the sauce through the pasta, then ladle on more sauce and the meatballs. Garnish with chopped parsley and grated cheddar and/or Parmesan. Leftovers go well in a lidded microwave box.

recipes.title: Marinara sauce
ingredients: Olive oil — 2 tbsp | 30 ml | 27 g | ⅛ UK cup | ⅛ US cup
Onion (finely chopped) — ½ medium | ~½ cup | 75 g
Tinned whole tomatoes — 2 x 28 oz can | 800 g
Fresh parsley or basil (optional, chopped) — 1 tbsp | 4 g
Water (optional) — up to 60 ml | ¼ cup, to thin if needed
steps: Blend the tomatoes: Tip the tinned whole tomatoes into a bowl (in batches if needed) and blend them as smooth or chunky as you like: chunkier for spaghetti sauce, smoother for pizza.

Soften the aromatics: Heat the olive oil over a low flame and cook the onion until translucent and soft but not coloured, then add the garlic and soften it. Add the salt, pepper and sugar (optional, to balance the acidity) and cook a couple of minutes.
Bloom the paste and herbs: Add the chilli flakes (optional) and a good heaped amount of tomato paste and cook briefly, then stir in the oregano and basil.
Add the tomatoes: Loosen the paste with some tomato juice, then stir in all the blended tomatoes.

Simmer: Cook low and slow, uncovered so it thickens, for about 40–45 minutes, stirring now and then. Add a little water if it gets too thick, and scrape the caramelised bits from the side of the pan back in.

Finish and store: Blend it smooth if you like, stir in fresh parsley or basil (optional), then cool and keep it in a jar or container in the fridge (the host says about 7 days). Use it as a base sauce for pasta, pizza or lasagne.

recipes.title: EASY Mini CHICKEN POT Pies
ingredients: 1 sheet (approx. 245g) refrigerated shortcrust pastry, how to make
2 Cooked chicken breast, diced or shredded or any chicken of choice
steps: Start the filling: In butter or olive oil, cook the diced onion and finely diced celery just to take the rawness out, with a little pepper (and the dried thyme from the description if you are using it). This comes together quickly.

Thicken: Stir in a couple of tablespoons of flour and cook the rawness out. Add the chicken broth, a heaped teaspoon of Dijon or English mustard (the description lists 1 tsp), and the cream (½ cup / 120 ml in the description). Add the cooked diced or shredded chicken and the frozen mixed vegetables (or peas, carrots or whatever you prefer). Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cook until thick: Let it simmer until you have a sauce thick enough for a pie — it will thicken more as it cools, so don't take it too far. Take it off the heat and let it cool.

Line the tins: Heat the oven to about 200°C (400°F). Roll the shortcrust (ready-rolled or homemade) to fit your mini tins, leaving a good inch and a half around so it comes up the sides. The host made at least four to start.

Fill and lid: Pack the tins generously with the cooled filling. Top with puff pastry, and use the beaten egg wash from the description. The captions don't linger on crimping or venting; watch that in the video rather than inventing steps.
Bake: Bake 25–30 minutes until the pastry is golden brown and puffed. Leave them about 10 minutes (or a little longer) before you cut one open.

recipes.title: Ham and Cheese Scones Biscuits – Tender, Cheesy & Easy to Bake
ingredients: All-purpose flour / Plain flour: 250g | 2 UK cups | 2 US cups
Cold butter, cubed: 60g | 4 tbsp | ¼ UK cup | ¼ US cup
Ham, finely diced: 100g | ⅔ UK cup | ¾ US cup
Cheddar cheese, shredded: 100g | 1 UK cup | 1 US cup
Fresh chives, or green onions chopped: 6g | 2 tbsp
Milk, cold: 120ml | ½ UK cup | ½ US cup
Full-fat Greek yogurt: 60g | ¼ UK cup | ¼ US cup
1 egg beaten with 1 tbsp milk (for golden tops)
steps: Prep: Preheat the oven. The host says about 180°C; the description says 200°C. Dice the ham, bigger if you want to see it, and chop the onion (or chives).
Dry mix: Whisk the flour, baking powder, mustard powder, salt, freshly ground black pepper and about ¼ teaspoon of garlic powder.
Rub in the butter: Rub the butter into the flour until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Wet mix: Beat the egg, then mix it with the Greek yogurt and milk.

Combine: Stir the ham, onion or chives and cheddar into the flour mix, then add the wet ingredients and bring it together. It will be quite wet. Turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and fold it over a couple of times without overworking or rolling it, so the scones stay light and moist.
Cut: Pat it out and cut straight down with a 3-inch cutter (about six scones), without twisting.

Top and bake: Brush the tops with milk, sprinkle each with a little cheddar and some Parmesan, and bake about 15–18 minutes, checking at 15, until golden and cooked. Serve warm with butter or alongside soup.

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F); Bake for 15–18 minutes until golden and cooked through.

recipes.title: EASY Strawberry Rhubarb Crumble Pie – Buttery & Delicious!
ingredients: 1 tsp vanilla extract or zest of 1/2 lemon (optional)
steps: Crumble pastry: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Beat the egg with the sugar, then mix in the melted butter, baking powder, salt (about ¼ tsp), the flour (280 g), and optional vanilla or lemon zest. Bring it together with your hands into a crumbly pastry — if it feels too wet, add a tablespoon more flour. It should be wet enough to press into a tin but still crumbly. Keep some back for the topping.

Cook part of the rhubarb: In a pan over a steady, not too high flame, cook 180 g of the chopped rhubarb with the sugar and a smidgeon of water to help it break down, plus a little lemon juice (1 tbsp in the description) to freshen it. Don't worry about the fluid — a tablespoon of cornflour / cornstarch will thicken it to a syrup. Stir in the remaining 70 g raw rhubarb for texture, then let the filling cool so you aren't working with it hot.
Strawberries: Mix the hulled, halved strawberries (250 g) with a little vanilla and the optional cinnamon, then combine with the cooled rhubarb.

Assemble: Press most of the pastry into the tin and up the sides — a measuring cup helps you squash it in — without overworking it. Tip in the filling, loosen the reserved pastry and scatter it over as a crumble top.
Bake: Bake about 35–40 minutes until the top is golden and the filling is bubbling. Serve warm with whipped cream or ice cream if you like.

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F); Bake for 35-40 minutes until the top is golden brown and the filling is bubbling.

recipes.title: EASY Yogurt PITA Bread – Stovetop for Perfect Pockets
ingredients: 250g (2 cups) all-purpose flour or bread flour
steps: Mix the dough: In a stand-mixer bowl, whisk the flour (a mix of bread and plain flour), sugar, yeast and salt, then add the water, yoghurt and olive oil.
Knead: Knead with a dough hook on low for 2–3 minutes, then one notch up for about 5–8 minutes in total, to a soft, sticky dough. It can also be done by hand.
First rise: With oiled hands, tuck the dough under into a ball, put it in an oiled bowl, cover and leave somewhere warm for about an hour until doubled.
Divide: On a lightly floured surface, divide into balls of about 70–75 g, rolling each one by pushing with your palm and pulling back with your fingers. Cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Roll: Roll each ball into an oval or round on a little flour.

Cook: Heat a dry pan on a low flame. Cook a pita until little bubbles appear, flip it, and keep flipping, pressing lightly with kitchen towel or a spatula so the steam lifts it into a pocket. Give it a little colour on both sides.
Keep soft: Stack the cooked pitas on a plate under a cover as you go so they stay moist. They freeze well; reheat in the microwave for about 20 seconds.

recipes.title: ONE TRAY Herb Roasted Chicken with Provençal Ratatouille
ingredients: 1 tsp dried oregano (1 g) (optional if no herbs de province)
½ tsp red pepper flakes (optional, 0.5 g)
¼ cup fresh basil (approx. 5 g), chopped optional
Salt and black pepper to taste
steps: Season the chicken: Drizzle the skin of the bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs with a little olive oil and season with salt, pepper and thyme (plus the garlic powder from the ingredient list). Season both sides if you like, then set aside. The heat comes from the description: 190°C (375°F).
Chop the veg: Cut the courgette (zucchini), red onion, peppers and aubergine into decent-sized chunks, or slices about ¼ inch thick. Don't cut them too small or they'll go mushy in 30–35 minutes.
Season the veg: Toss the veg with olive oil (the aubergine soaks it up), salt, pepper and a good heaped spoon of herbes de Provence or mixed herbs, using your hands.
Assemble the tray: Spread the veg on a tray (lined if you like), sit the chicken on top, and dot the cherry tomatoes around, on the vine if you have them.
Roast: Roast for about 30–35 minutes (the description says until the chicken reaches 75°C/165°F inside and the veg are tender and lightly golden).
Serve: Serve on rice with a little parsley (or fresh basil).

recipes.title: Classic Beef and Mushrooms Suet Pudding - Old-School Comfort Food!
ingredients: Stewing beef (chuck or shin, diced) — 500g | 1.1 lb | 2 cups (UK & US)
Chestnut or button mushrooms (sliced, diced thick) — 400g | 14 oz
Dried thyme — 1 pinch | about ¼ tsp | 0.5g
Cold water — 60ml | 4 tbsp | ¼ cup (UK & US), plus more if needed
Let pressure naturally release for 10 minutes, then quick release.
Quick release, lift out the basin, rest for 5 mins, then turn out and serve.
Simmer the filling on the stove or oven for 2–2½ hours. Steam the pudding in a large covered pot for 2½ to 3 hours, topping up with boiling water as needed.
steps: Season and flour the beef: This is the only time the host seasons the meat. Coat the diced stewing beef (shin or chuck, about 500 g) with salt and pepper, then flour it so it fries with a caramelized crust and helps thicken the gravy later.

Fry and build the filling: Heat a little oil, and about a tablespoon of butter if you like. Brown the floured beef, then cook the chopped onion and garlic just to take the rawness out, and add the sliced mushrooms (400 g), mixed herbs, a little more salt and pepper, about a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce, about a tablespoon of tomato purée, and the beef stock (250 ml in the description).

Cook the filling: Pressure-cook on high about 25 minutes (the host also says 25–30), then natural release 10 minutes before you vent. Without an Instant Pot, simmer on the stove or in the oven 2–2½ hours. When it is done, lift out the meat and mushrooms and thicken the gravy with a cornflour slurry — 1 tablespoon cornflour mixed with 1 tablespoon water — either on sauté mode or in a pan, so the filling isn't too runny inside the pudding.

Suet pastry: Mix the self-raising flour with a pinch of dried thyme and the salt. Rub in about 40 g cold cubed butter (optional, but the host likes the flavor) and about 100 g shredded suet. Add about 4 tablespoons of cold water, plus a little more if needed, to make a dough.

Line, fill and cover: Butter the basin well. Roll the pastry with a little flour so it fits the basin with a slight overhang, line it, add the filling, and roll a lid to cover. Traditionally you'd put foil on and tie it with string; for the Instant Pot the host just squashes the foil around the basin.

Steam: Sit the basin on the trivet and pressure-cook on high 45 minutes, then quick release, rest about 5 minutes and turn it out. On the stove, steam in a large covered pot 2½ to 3 hours, topping up with boiling water as needed.

recipes.title: LEMON Yogurt TRAYBAKE  Cake
ingredients: Plain flour — 180 g | 1½ UK cups | 1½ US cups
Caster sugar — 200 g | 1 UK cup | 1 US cup
Plain or Greek yogurt — 180 g | 180 ml | ¾ UK cup | ¾ US cup see below
Vegetable oil — 110 g | 120 ml | ½ UK cup | ½ US cup
Fresh lemon juice — 55 g | 60 ml | ¼ UK cup | ¼ US cup
Icing sugar — 120 g | 1 UK cup | 1 US cup
Fresh lemon juice — 30–45 ml | 2–3 tbsp (adjust for desired thickness)
steps: Prep: Line a 9×11 inch tray (or 9×13 inch for a thinner cake) with parchment and heat the oven to about 175–180°C (160°C fan).
Dry ingredients: Mix the plain flour, baking powder and salt.
Wet ingredients: Beat the Greek yoghurt, sugar, vanilla and lemon zest with the eggs and oil from the ingredient list, then beat in the lemon juice.
Fold: Fold in the flour mixture until there are no clumps.
Bake: Pour into the tray, level it, and bake for 25–35 minutes, checking from about 25–28 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Leave in the tray for 10 minutes, then cool on a rack.

Cut and glaze: Put the cake on a board with parchment and cut it into squares first, loosening them a little apart. Mix the icing sugar with lemon juice, drizzle or spread it over the top so it runs down between the squares, and add a little lemon zest before it dries.

recipes.title: OLD Fashioned WET CAKE - Sticky BRITISH Fruit Cake NO Butter or Oil
ingredients: Strong black tea (e.g. English Breakfast) — 300ml | 1¼ cups (UK & US) | 20 tbsp fluid
Brown sugar (light or dark) — 120g | ¾ cup (UK) | ¾ cup (US) | 8 tbsp
Optional: Zest of 1 orange or lemon
Pour over the 300ml (1¼ cups) of freshly brewed strong black tea. Cover and let soak overnight (or at least 6 hours) at room temperature.
steps: Soak the fruit: Pour the strong black tea (no milk or sugar) over the sultanas and currants, cover and leave overnight until plump. As a shortcut, microwave the fruit and hot tea for 3 minutes, cover with cling wrap and leave 1 hour.
Prepare: Preheat the oven (180°C, or 160°C fan in the description) and line a 2 lb loaf tin.

Mix: Put the fruit and all the remaining tea in a bowl with the brown sugar and mix to break up any clumps. Stir in a teaspoon of mixed spice (the host leaves out the optional cinnamon), then the beaten egg, the orange or lemon zest (optional) and a pinch of salt.
Add the flour: Mix in the self-raising flour until no dry flour is left and you have a batter. Don't overmix.
Bake: Scrape it into the tin. Smoothing the top is optional. Bake about 50–60 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool: Leave it in the tin briefly, then turn it out onto a rack. Serve warm or cold, sliced thick with butter (or cheese) and a cup of tea.

recipes.title: LEMON YOGHURT Pound Cake – Moist, Buttery & Irresistibly Citrusy
ingredients: 250g (1 cup) full-fat Greek yoghurt — see note below to make at home
250g (2 cups) cake flour (sifted) see note to make at home
Mix 100g (¾ cup) icing sugar with 2 tbsp lemon juice and drizzle over the cooled cake for an extra zesty finish.
steps: Prep: Put a liner in a 2 lb loaf tin and heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).

Blend the wet ingredients: In a blender (or by hand), blend the yoghurt, sugar, eggs, lemon juice, about 1½ teaspoons of vanilla, the salt, lemon zest and melted butter for only about a minute to a smooth batter.
Add the flour: Add the sifted cake flour, with the baking powder from the ingredient list, and mix just until combined.
Bake: Pour the batter into the middle of the tin and let it find its own way out, then bake (the description gives 45–55 minutes) until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool: Leave it in the tin for 10 minutes, lift it out, remove the paper and let it cool completely.

Ice: Set the cake on parchment. Stir the icing sugar with a little lemon juice until smooth, spoon it over the top so it runs down the sides, finish with lemon zest if you have it, and let it set before slicing.

recipes.title: The Secret to Perfect Pan Fried Pork Chops – Ready in 10 Minutes!
ingredients: Dried thyme — ½ tsp (or 1 tsp fresh, finely chopped)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Chicken broth (or white wine) — ¼ cup
Mashed potatoes, to serve, made as you would usually.
steps: Season the chops: Use 2–4 bone-in pork chops, about an inch thick. Season both sides with salt, pepper, smoked paprika, dried thyme and optional rosemary.

Sear: Heat a little olive oil in a pan (a high-sided one is handy) and, when it is hot, add the chops. Sear about 4–5 minutes per side until golden. You can turn them sooner if you need to, but aim for that sort of time each side. Then stand them on the fatty edge for a couple of minutes so that edge crisps too. They should feel slightly firm, not rock hard. The description gives 145°F / 63°C inside.

Rest and make the sauce: Take the chops out to rest and turn the flame down. Add some butter to the pan and cook the minced garlic just to take the rawness out — don't burn it. Stir in about a teaspoon of whole-grain mustard (Dijon is fine if you prefer), then about ¼ cup chicken stock or white wine. Keep the heat lowish.
Finish: Return the chops and any juices to the pan to coat in the garlic-butter sauce. Serve with mashed potatoes if you like. It isn't a creamy sauce — just a quick pan sauce.

recipes.title: Easy ONE POT Chicken CHASSEUR – HUNTERS Chicken
ingredients: 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (or a mix of thighs and drumsticks)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
1 shallot or ½ small onion, finely chopped
150g (5 oz) mushrooms, sliced minimum I use 250g
120ml (½ cup) white wine (dry, such as Sauvignon Blanc)
1 sprig thyme (or ½ tsp dried thyme)
steps: Season, then flour: Season the skin-on, bone-in chicken thighs with salt and pepper first, then dust them with flour. Seasoning the flour instead loses half the seasoning.
Brown: Heat oil and butter in a pan over a moderate flame and brown the chicken skin side down, turning a couple of times, for about 3–4 minutes a side. Remove it.

Onion and mushrooms: In the same pan, gently sauté the finely diced onion with little colour, add a bit more butter, then the sliced or halved mushrooms (use plenty, as they shrink). Cook until coloured, then add the garlic.

Wine and seasonings: Add the white wine (optional; brandy also works) and let it reduce a minute. Add about a teaspoon each of Worcestershire sauce and Dijon mustard, plus the tomato paste from the ingredient list.

Tomatoes and stock: Add the tinned tomatoes with their juice, then the chicken stock, and bring it back up to temperature. Add about a teaspoon of sugar to balance the sourness, plus the bay leaf, tarragon and thyme.
Simmer: Return the chicken, turn down to a simmer, cover and cook for about 10–15 minutes. Then take the lid off and simmer for another 5–10 minutes to reduce and thicken the sauce.
Serve: Sprinkle with parsley and serve over rice or with mashed potato.

recipes.title: UK Chinese Takeaway Style Special Curry
ingredients: Beef (steak or brisket), sliced — 100g | 3.5 oz I used sirloin/striploin

Oyster sauce (or mushroom sauce for veg) — 1 tbsp | 15ml
Water or chicken stock — 250ml | 1 UK cup | 1.06 US cups
Cornflour (for slurry) — 1 tbsp | 8g mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Marinate the beef: Mix the sliced beef with a little soy sauce, white pepper and sesame oil and leave for about 15 minutes (longer if you like).
Blanch the proteins: Bring a pan of water to the boil and blanch the sliced chicken and beef for about a minute, then the shrimp (fresh or frozen) last so they don't overcook. Drain and set aside.
Fry the veg: Heat a little oil and fry some carrot for colour (optional), the green pepper, onion, and a little garlic and ginger. Add the peas.

Make the sauce: Add about 2½ tablespoons of Chinese curry paste with water or chicken stock and a drizzle of sesame oil. If you don't have the paste, use the curry powder, flour, soy, oyster sauce and sugar version from the ingredient list. Bring it up so it starts to thicken.
Add the meat: Add the chicken, beef and sliced char siu pork and cook until the sauce is as thick as you like. Stir the prawns through last and turn off the heat.
Serve: Serve over fried rice.

recipes.title: EASY Restaurant Style Char Siu Pork - Home Style!
ingredients: 3 tablespoons (45 ml / 45 g / 9 tsp) Lee Kum Kee Char Siu Sauce
1 teaspoon (5 ml / 5 g) light soy sauce (optional, for added savoury depth)
1/4 teaspoon (a few drops) red food colouring (optional, for that classic red tint)

steps: Marinate: Mix the Char Siu sauce (the host uses Lee Kum Kee, 3 tablespoons in the description) with about a teaspoon of light soy sauce if you want extra savoury depth, and optional red food colouring — the description lists ¼ teaspoon; the host talks about about ½ teaspoon. Coat a pork tenderloin (about 450 g). Refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight; the host only had about 4 hours on this cook and said it was still fine.

Roast on a rack: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) / 400°F. Sit the pork on a rack over a roasting tray with 2–3 tablespoons of water underneath so the juices don't burn. There is no basting or extra glaze — the marinade does the work.

recipes.title: ULTIMATE Cheesy Mashed Potato Soup Roll - EASY Soft Fluffy
ingredients: Bread flour — 500g (3⅓ UK cups / 4⅛ US cups) I used 250g plain/all-purpose - 250g Bread flour
A little milk for brushing before baking
Melted unsalted butter — 2–3 tbsp (for brushing after baking)
Cover and proof for 1 hour or until doubled in size.
Cover and let rise for 30–40 minutes until puffed and touching.
steps: Make the dough: In a stand mixer, combine 250 g plain flour and 250 g bread flour with the sugar, salt, yeast, egg, warm milk and melted butter. Mix slowly with a dough hook, then increase the speed slightly and knead for 8 minutes (or by hand).
First rise: Put the dough in a bowl, cover and leave somewhere warm for about 1–1½ hours until doubled.

Make the mash: Boil the potatoes (peeled or not) in salted water, drain and mash with the warmed cream or milk, salt and pepper. Let it go cold, then mix in finely sliced spring onion. Hot mash would make the dough split.
Portion: Divide the dough into 12 balls of about 70 g each. Use about the same weight of filling for each.
Fill and seal: Flatten each ball, add a portion of mash and some grated mozzarella, bring the edges up and pinch them firmly to seal. Place seam side down in a lined 10×10 inch tray.
Second rise: Cover and rise for about 40 minutes until puffed and touching.
Bake: Brush with a little milk and bake at 180°C (350°F) (the description gives 25–30 minutes) until golden.
Butter and cool: Brush with melted butter as soon as they come out, leave 10 minutes in the tray, then slide them off the paper onto a rack. Tear and share, perfect with soup.

recipes.title: Creamy Broccoli Cheddar Chicken Orzo – A One Pan Dinner Favourite
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
2 cloves garlic, minced (approx. 1 tsp or 5 g)
1/2 tsp (1 g) smoked paprika (optional, for extra flavour)
1 cup (200 g, UK: 220 ml / US: 240 ml) orzo pasta
2 cups (480 ml, UK: 450 ml / US: 480 ml) low-sodium chicken broth
1 cup (240 ml, UK: 250 ml / US: 240 ml) whole milk (or half-and-half for extra creaminess) I used Evaporated Milk
2 cups (180 g,) broccoli florets, cut into small pieces
1 1/2 cups (170 g) shredded sharp cheddar cheese
1/2 tsp (2.5 g) Dijon mustard (optional, enhances cheesy flavour)
1/4 tsp (0.5 g) red pepper flakes (optional, for a slight kick)
steps: Brown the chicken: In a little olive oil and butter, cook the bite-size chicken with a little salt (not much — the stock is salty even if it is low-sodium) and about ½ tsp smoked paprika (the host started to say a teaspoon, then used half). Get some colour on it, then take the chicken out, leaving the flavoured oil in the pan. The sticky bits can come out if you want; the host leaves the flavour in the oil.
Toast the orzo: Add the orzo and toast 1–2 minutes until it takes on a little golden colour and picks up the pan flavour.

Simmer: Pour in the chicken stock and the milk — the host uses evaporated milk instead of whole milk or half-and-half. Bring it up to a good simmer, stirring, so the pasta can absorb the liquid. Stir in about a teaspoon of Dijon mustard (the description lists ½ tsp).

Broccoli and finish: Lid on and let it cook. Add the small broccoli florets for the last few minutes (the host says there are still a couple of minutes to go on the broccoli), and red pepper flakes if you like. Return the chicken to the pan to heat through — if the captions skip the exact moment, watch that in the video rather than inventing a time.

Cheese: Off the heat, stir in a tablespoon of butter, the sharp cheddar and the Parmesan if using. It will thicken in about 2 minutes. Serve with a little extra cheddar and a tiny bit of parsley if you like. The host says the whole meal takes about 25–30 minutes.

recipes.title: EASY Soft and Fluffy DINNER ROLLS – PERFECT for Any Meal!
ingredients: Flour: 500g (4 cups UK, 4 1/8 cups US) bread flour or all-purpose/plain flour - I used 250 all-purpose/plain flour and 250 bread flour
Sugar: 50g (4 tbsp UK, 3 ½ tbsp US) granulated sugar
Instant Yeast: 7g (2 ¼ tsp) or active dry yeast (proof in warm milk)
Milk: 250ml (1 cup UK, 1 cup US) warm whole milk (38-40°C / 100-105°F)
Butter: 60g (4 tbsp UK, 3 ½ tbsp US) softened, unsalted butter
Milk or egg wash: 1 tbsp milk or 1 egg beaten with 1 tbsp water
Melted butter: 30g (2 tbsp UK, 1 ¾ tbsp US) for brushing after baking
steps: Mix the dry ingredients: In a stand-mixer bowl, mix 250 g bread flour and 250 g plain flour (split for softer rolls) with the sugar, salt and yeast.
Add the wet ingredients: Add the egg, softened butter and warm milk.

Knead: Using a dough hook, mix on low until combined, then increase the speed slightly and knead for about 7–8 minutes (or about 10 minutes by hand). The dough should be tacky, soft and springy but not overly sticky.
First rise: Shape into a ball, put it in a lightly buttered bowl, cover and leave somewhere warm to double in size, about an hour or so.
Shape: Knock it back gently and divide into 12 pieces of about 73–75 g. Roll each into a ball by pushing with your palm and pulling back with your fingers. Place in a lined 10×10 inch tray.
Second rise: Cover and leave for about 40 minutes until puffy.
Bake: Bake at 180°C (350°F) for about 18–22 minutes until golden.
Brush and cool: Brush with melted butter straight away, leave in the tray for about 10 minutes, then slide them off the paper onto a rack.

recipes.title: SLOW Cooker GREEK Yogurt - FOOLPROOF Method!
ingredients: 2 litres (8 cups) of whole milk (or use 2% milk, but whole milk gives creamier yoghurt)
2 tbsp plain yoghurt with live active cultures (as a starter) I used probiotic
Heat the milk to 82°C (180°F), stirring occasionally to prevent scorching.
steps: Heat the milk: Pour the whole milk into the slow cooker, put the lid on and switch it on. Heat it to about 82–83°C. In the video this took about 2½ hours; check the temperature after about 2 hours.
Cool: Turn the slow cooker off and let the milk cool to about 43°C (46°C was used here). This takes hours.
Add the starter: Loosen live probiotic yoghurt with a little of the warm milk, using about 1 tablespoon per litre of milk, then stir it gently through all the milk.
Incubate: Put the lid back on and, with the slow cooker off, wrap it snugly in a towel. Leave it undisturbed for about 9 hours or overnight.
Chill: Spoon the set yoghurt into tubs and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.

Make Greek yoghurt: For Greek style, line a sieve set over a bowl with a cotton cloth (cheesecloth), spoon in the yoghurt and let the whey drain in the fridge for at least 4 hours or overnight. Keep the whey for baking or pour it on your plants.

recipes.title: IRISH Stew SODA Bread Bowls – The ULTIMATE Cosy Comfort Food
ingredients: For the Mini Soda Bread Loaves (Bowls):
400ml (1 ⅔ cups) buttermilk (or milk + 1 tbsp lemon juice/vinegar)
1 tbsp soft butter (optional, for a softer crust)
For the Instant Pot Irish Stew:
500g (1.1 lbs) lamb or beef, cut into bite-sized chunks, I used shin beef
125ml (½ cup) Guinness stout or extra stock (optional)
1 tbsp cornstarch + 2 tbsp water (optional, for thickening)
steps: Coat the beef: Season the cubed beef (the host uses shin) with salt and pepper and toss it with a couple of tablespoons of flour.
Brown the beef: Brown it in a little oil in a frying pan, which gives more control than the Instant Pot's sauté setting, just to get colour. Transfer it to the Instant Pot.
Start the veg: In the same pan, add butter, then the onion and garlic, then the carrots and leek, just to give them a start. Add about a teaspoon of thyme and scrape up the browned bits.

Pressure cook: Add the veg and potatoes to the pot with the beef stock, Guinness, Worcestershire sauce and a couple of bay leaves, and mix. Pressure cook on high for 45 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 15 minutes. On the hob, simmer it covered for about 1½–2 hours instead.

Make the soda bread: Mix the flour, about a teaspoon of salt and the baking soda, add the buttermilk and bring it together by hand into a sticky dough. Divide it into four (or six) on a floured surface without kneading, shape roughly, cut a cross in each top and put them on a parchment-lined tray.
Bake: Bake about 30–35 minutes (the description says 20–25 at 200°C) until they sound hollow underneath. While hot, rub the tops with butter and cover with kitchen paper so they steam and soften.
Make the bowls: Slice off the tops, cut around inside the crust and pull out the middle, going close to the bottom without breaking through. Keep the bread for dipping.
Fill: Vent the remaining pressure, then put a piece of the removed bread in the bottom of each bowl and ladle in the stew. Garnish with parsley and serve with the buttered tops and bread for dipping.

Layer the dish: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). recipes.title: Mince & Tatties CLASSIC SCOTTISH comfort food with A TWIST
ingredients: 2 tsp cornflour (cornstarch) mixed with 2 tbsp water (for thickening) as needed
800g (1¾ lbs) potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
150g ( 1 cup) self-raising flour — All purpose/ Plain flour works, I only had self-raising
steps: Start the tatties: Get the potatoes on to boil so they can cook while you make the mince. When they are done, drain, return them to the pan to dry off, then mash with butter, milk, and salt and pepper to taste. No oil in the mash.

Brown the mince: Have the oven on if you are making giant Yorkshire puddings (the description says 230°C / 460°F). In a little oil (or butter if you want), cook the onion, carrot and garlic to take the rawness out, then add the beef mince, break it up and cook it down. Season with pepper and rosemary salt (or ordinary salt) — the host holds back extra salt at this stage because of the rosemary salt.

Make the gravy: Stir in about a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce and a heaped tablespoon of tomato puree, then the beef stock or a stock cube. The description lists 1000 ml (4 cups) stock; the host says about 500 ml of gravy will do for the mince, onions, carrots and mash, and you can add a little more water if you need it. Let it cook about 5 minutes. A cornflour slurry is listed in the description if you need to thicken; use it only as needed.

Suet dumplings: Mix self-raising flour with shredded suet (or butter if you can't use suet) and a little salt. Start with about 2 tablespoons of cold water and add another if you need it — flours differ, so don't tip in a large amount at once. The description lists 3–4 tbsp. Sit the dumplings on the mince, lid on, and cook 20 minutes. (If you were serving plain mince and tatties, you would just cook until the carrots are soft and the mince is done, then serve with the mash.)

Giant Yorkshire puddings (the twist): Whisk self-raising or plain flour with 3–4 eggs, 175 ml milk, a tad of water (the description also lists 25 ml) and a pinch of salt. The water helps them puff and crisp. Warm the tins in the oven, then add a splash of oil or beef dripping, let the fat get hot, and pour in the batter. The description gives 20 minutes at 230°C (460°F).
Serve: Spoon the mince and dumplings with the tatties, or serve it in the giant Yorkshire puddings.

recipes.title: Pan Fried CHCKEN Creamy Smoked BACON Sauce & CORNBREAD
ingredients: 2 large boneless, skinless chicken breasts (split into 4 cutlets)

4-5 medium carrots, peeled and cut into thick sticks

steps: Cornbread batter: Preheat the oven (200°C in the description). Mix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, salt and sugar, then add the eggs, buttermilk and melted butter and stir to combine. Jalapeños are optional. Pour into a lined 8×8-inch tin.

Carrots: Toss the carrots (the host halves baby carrots) with olive oil, rosemary salt, smoked paprika and the maple syrup, with a little butter in the pan if you like. Put both the cornbread and the carrots in the oven for about 25–30 minutes, until the cornbread is golden rather than brown.

Turn it again and season with garlic powder and smoked paprika, turning so both sides get colour and flavour. Cook through, then take it out and cover it with foil.

Start the sauce: Wipe out any burnt bits left in the pan, keeping some of the flavour. Soften the onion and garlic, then add the smoked bacon and cook until coloured, or crisp if you prefer. Set a few pieces aside for garnish.

recipes.title: Strawberry Cotton Cheesecake with Jelly – A Dreamy Layered Dessert!
ingredients: 250g (9oz or 1¾ cups) fresh or frozen strawberries
6g (2 tsp) powdered gelatine, bloomed with 30ml (2 tbsp) cold water
8g (2½ tsp) powdered gelatine, bloomed with 30ml (2 tbsp) cold water
Optional: ½ tsp strawberry liqueur (e.g., strawberry schnapps or crème de fraise) for extra depth
steps: Cotton sponge: Preheat the oven — the description says 170°C (340°F). Whisk the egg yolks with the warm milk, oil and vanilla, and sieve in the cake flour. In another bowl, beat the egg whites with a pinch of salt, then gradually add the sugar until the mixture is light and foamy. Fold the whites into the yolk batter until just combined. Pour into a 24 × 34 cm pan and bake about 20–25 minutes (the description says 20–22 minutes) until golden and springy. Cool in the tray a little, then cut a piece to fit your tin — the host uses a 6-inch (15 cm) loose-bottom tin and uses the tin as a guide.

Strawberry coulis: Cook the strawberries with the sugar and lemon juice about 7 minutes, then blend and sieve out the seeds. Let it cool. You'll use this for the cream layer, the jelly, and a syrup to moisten the sponge (3 tbsp coulis with 2 tbsp water in the description, and an optional splash of strawberry liqueur).

Cream cheese layer: Soften the cream cheese with the sugar. Bloom the gelatine in 2 tablespoons of cold water (6 g gelatine in the description). Mix with the cold heavy cream and 100 g (½ cup) of the cooled coulis. The captions don't spell out every mixer's speed; watch the video for that rather than inventing a whipping method.

Layer and set: In the loose-bottom tin, add about half of the cream cheese mixture, moisten the sponge with the syrup, sit the sponge on top, then add the rest of the cream cheese mixture and spread it to the edges. Refrigerate about 15–20 minutes until it is starting to set.

Jelly topping: Bloom 8 g gelatine with 2 tablespoons of water, then mix it with 80 g (⅓ cup) of coulis and 75 ml (⅓ cup) water. Pour this over the set cream layer and refrigerate until the jelly is set (the host talks about another 20 minutes, then finishing). Decorate with a few small strawberries if you like.

recipes.title: How to make PERFECT GREEK Yoghurt  - Thick, Tangy & Foolproof!
ingredients: 1 liter (4 cups) whole milk (or 2% for a lighter yogurt)

recipes.title: DO NOT BE SOLD SHORT How to Make Heavy Cream from Milk and Butter Whippable & Stable!
ingredients: Xanthan Gum: ½ tsp (helps emulsify and stabilize)
Lecithin (Optional): ½ tsp (either soy or sunflower lecithin, helps maintain emulsion)
Gelatin (Optional for Better Whipping): ½ tsp powdered gelatin + 1 tbsp cold water
steps: Bloom the gelatin: Stir ½ teaspoon of gelatin into 1 tablespoon of cold water and leave 5 minutes to bloom (or microwave about 5 seconds). Agar works instead of gelatin.

Blend: Put the whole milk in a blender. With it running on low, pour in the melted butter, then add ½ teaspoon of xanthan gum, ½ teaspoon of soy lecithin, the bloomed gelatin and the pinch of salt (optional). Blend about a minute.
Chill: Pour it into an airtight container and refrigerate at least 8 hours or overnight. It keeps up to 5 days in the fridge.
Whip: Make sure everything is cold, then whip the cream to firm peaks. It holds its shape for 12–24 hours. Add powdered sugar for dessert cream, which also masks the slight butter taste.

recipes.title: APPLE CHEESECAKE PIE – Buttery Crust, Spiced Apples & Creamy Filling
ingredients: 1 ½ cups (180g) graham cracker crumbs (or digestive biscuits, finely crushed)
¼ cup (50g) granulated sugar 25g if using digestive
2 medium apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced (Granny Smith or Honeycrisp work well)

Thicken with a little cornstarch or a slurry if you need to (1 tsp is listed as optional). Let this topping cool.

Streusel (optional but recommended): Rub the flour, brown sugar, cinnamon and butter together (melted or cold, cubed). If the mix is too wet, add a little more flour. A pinch of salt can go in; that isn't in the description.

Finish: Spoon the apples over the cheesecake, add the streusel, and bake about 20–25 minutes (the host says about 20) until the apples are tender and the streusel is golden. Cool completely, then refrigerate about 3 hours (the host served his after a couple of hours). Caramel sauce is listed if you want to dress it.

recipes.title: GREEK CHICKEN Gyros with Homemade Tzatziki Sauce & Flatbread QUICK & Easy
ingredients: 2 large chicken breasts, cut into strips
1 cup Greek yogurt (full-fat for best texture)
4 pita breads or flatbreads — or make your own – recipe below
1/4 cup crumbled feta (optional, for extra creaminess)
1 tablespoon (15ml) olive oil (optional, for softer texture)
steps: Marinate the chicken: Cut 2 large chicken breasts into strips and mix with olive oil, minced garlic, dried oregano, smoked paprika, optional cumin (the captions mention cumin going in; it's listed as optional in the description), salt, pepper, about ½ teaspoon lemon zest and about a tablespoon of lemon juice. Tzatziki: Grate ½ cucumber and squeeze it dry. Mix with the Greek yogurt, minced garlic, chopped fresh dill or mint, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper. Refrigerate while you make the bread and cook the chicken.

Flatbreads: Mix 250 g self-raising flour with 180 g Greek yogurt, optional salt and a little olive oil. Knead a few minutes until it comes together, rest briefly, then divide into about four, cover and rest about 10 minutes more. Roll them out with a little flour and cook in a pan over a moderate, not crazy-high, heat. The captions don't dwell on exact times per side; watch the video and cook until they are done and spotted.
Cook the chicken: Grill or pan-cook the marinated strips until they're cooked through, turning when they start to go opaque. Rest them in a tin under foil about 2–3 minutes while you assemble.
Assemble: Warm the flatbreads or pittas, add the chicken, tzatziki, diced tomatoes, diced red onion, chopped parsley, optional crumbled feta, and lemon wedges.

recipes.title: EASY Cherry Crumble Pie – Buttery Crust & Sweet Cherry Filling
ingredients: 150g unsalted butter, cold & cubed — I use melted - if you cold rub in like pastry

50g sugar (optional, if the filling is not sweet enough)
steps: Make the dough: Whisk the egg with the sugar, a pinch of salt and the vanilla, then stir in the melted butter. Add the flour and baking powder and bring it together with the whisk, then by hand, into a moist but crumbly dough. Add a sprinkle of flour if it is too wet, without drying it out.
Divide: Keep about a third for the crumble topping and use two-thirds for the base. Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Make the filling: Mix about a tablespoon of cornflour with some of the juice from the pie filling, then stir it into the rest. Press in the base: Press the two-thirds of dough into a pie dish of about 26 cm, smoothing the bottom and pushing it up the sides with a spoon, measuring cup or glass. No rolling needed.
Fill and top: Pour in the cherry filling, then crumble the remaining dough over the top with your hands, almost to the edges.

recipes.title: Ultimate IRISH CORNED BEEF & Cabbage WELLINGTON
ingredients: Cooked corned beef, shredded or chopped — 350 g
Cabbage, thinly sliced — ½ small head
Mashed potatoes, seasoned with salt and pepper — 200 g
Milk — 250 ml (1 cup) (or half milk, half stock)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
steps: Mash the potatoes: Boil and mash them as you usually would, with a little butter and milk if you want, and salt and pepper to taste. The filling needs to be cool, so get this done and let it cool. The description lists 200 g seasoned mashed potatoes.

An egg wash is listed in the description; use it if you are glazing the pastry.

recipes.title: Pepperoni Pizza Layer Cake
ingredients: 2 pre-made pizza crusts (store-bought or homemade, about 25 cm / 10 inches each)
200 g (2 cups) shredded mozzarella cheese or cheese of choice
225 g (1 cup) cooked ground beef (seasoned with ½ tsp salt & ½ tsp black pepper)
120 ml (½ cup) extra pizza sauce (for layering)

steps: Brown the beef: In a little oil over a not-too-hot pan, cook the diced onion and minced garlic, and brown the cooked or raw ground beef with a little colour (225 g, seasoned with ½ tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper in the description) and a heaped teaspoon of Italian herbs.

ingredients: 1 tsp vanilla extract (5ml) stirred in when making batter - (bad edit - not shown)

recipes.title: Bang Bang Chicken Skewers – Sweet, Spicy & Irresistibly Juicy!
ingredients: 1 ½ lbs (680g) boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1-inch cubes
½ tsp ground ginger (adds a subtle warmth)
Wooden skewers (soaked in water for 30 minutes)

steps: Make the dough: Mix the eggs, oil, softened butter, sugar and vanilla (vanilla sugar is in the description) with all-purpose flour and baking powder. recipes.title: Crispy Arabic Spinach Rolls – Easy & Delicious Middle Eastern Fatayer Sabanekh
ingredients: 60-80g Spreadable white cheese: 3-4 tablespoons cream cheese would work well as a substitute. You could also use Labneh or ricotta for a more traditional touch.
120-150g Crumbled white cheese (feta, Akkawi, or similar)
Mix feta with a bit of cream cheese or ricotta to make it creamier.
steps: Make the dough: Dissolve the salt in the warm water, then add the flour and knead about 8 minutes in a stand mixer, or by hand for 8–10 minutes, adding the flour a bit at a time. You want a slightly sticky dough.
First rest: Shape it into a ball, put it in a lightly floured bowl (no oil), cover and rest 30 minutes.
Divide: On a floured surface, divide the dough into about eight equal pieces, shape them into balls, and cover them in a box for about 15 minutes.
Salt the spinach: Chop the washed spinach and mix it with about a teaspoon of salt. Leave about 5 minutes, stirring once, to draw out the liquid.
Grease the dough: Mix the melted butter with the vegetable oil. Roll out each ball a little, coat it with the butter-oil mix and stack them on a plate.
Make the filling: Wearing gloves, squeeze as much liquid as you can from the spinach. Mix in the chilli flakes, chopped onion, feta and the creamy cheese (ricotta, cream cheese or labneh).

Stretch: Oil the work surface, lay a piece of dough on it and stretch it out with your fingers until paper-thin, the way rotis are made; small tears don't matter. Trim the edge straight with a pizza wheel and fold it over on itself to make layers.
Fill and roll: Spoon filling along one edge, fold the dough over and roll it up like a sausage roll, tucking in the sides as you go. Put it on a parchment-lined tray and repeat.
Bake: Brush the tops lightly with more butter-oil mix and bake at 190–200°C until golden and crisp (35–40 minutes in the description). Cool 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Easy Chicken Broccoli Rice Casserole with Cheesy Crunchy Topping
ingredients: 1.5 lbs boneless skinless chicken breast, cut, bite-sized pieces
4 cups broccoli florets, cut into bite-sized pieces
½ cup panko breadcrumbs (for extra crunch)
steps: Steam the broccoli: Bring a little water to the boil in a pan, set a small colander or sieve of broccoli florets on top, cover with a lid and steam 5–6 minutes until a fork goes in but they are still firm. Tip them into a large bowl. (If you are cooking rice from scratch instead of using cooked rice, you can add the broccoli for the last 5 minutes.)

Cook the chicken: In the same pan, melt a little butter and cook the onion and garlic just to take the rawness out. Add the diced chicken and cook about 5 minutes, a little longer if any pink remains, until it puffs up and is just cooked; it finishes in the oven. Turn the heat off and add the chicken, onion and juices to the broccoli.

Make the cheese sauce: Melt about 4 tablespoons of butter, stir in about 4 tablespoons of flour and cook out the rawness. Add the herbs and seasonings, then pour in all the milk followed by the cream, with the Dijon, a little pepper and a little salt. Cook until it thickens, which doesn't take long. Turn the heat off and stir in most of the cheddar, keeping some for the top. It doesn't need to be completely smooth.
Loosen the sauce: If the sauce is thick, stir in the chicken stock. Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Make the topping: Crush the Ritz crackers and mix them with the panko breadcrumbs.
Assemble: Add the cooked rice to the chicken and broccoli, pour over the cheese sauce and mix. Spread it in a baking dish, cover with the cracker crumbs and top with the reserved cheddar.
Bake: Bake about 25 minutes until bubbling and golden. If you like, push a few pieces of broccoli into the top for show at the end, so they don't burn in the oven.
Serve: The top sets into a crust, so cut a portion, lift the crust off, spoon out the filling, then put the crust back on top.

recipes.title: STEAK and Onion Pie with FORGOTTEN Suet Crust
ingredients: For the Pie Filling (Instant Pot Version):
Salt and black pepper, to taste
400ml beef stock (more liquid for stove top 600ml)
1 tbsp cornstarch + 2 tbsp water (slurry, if needed)
1 tbsp butter + 1 tbsp oil for frying
Pressure cook on HIGH for 35 minutes.
Let it naturally release for 10 minutes, then quick release any remaining pressure.
steps: Brown the steak: Season 1 kg cubed stewing steak (topside or chuck) and fry it in about a tablespoon of oil and a tablespoon of butter until it has some colour. The host prefers a pan to the Instant Pot's sauté mode because he finds that too hot, but use sauté if you like. Tip the beef into the Instant Pot (or a casserole if you're cooking on the stove) and leave the browned bits in the pan.

Onions and gravy: Add a little more butter and cook the sliced onions and optional minced garlic just to take the rawness out — keep some texture. Add them to the beef with dried thyme, about a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce, 1½ tbsp tomato purée, a little salt and pepper, and the beef stock (400 ml for the Instant Pot; the description suggests 600 ml on the stove).

Cook the filling: Pressure-cook on high 35 minutes, then natural release 10 minutes before you vent. On the stove, simmer about 2 hours until the beef is tender. If the gravy needs thickening, mix a little of it with a cornstarch slurry (1 tbsp cornstarch + 2 tbsp water in the description) and stir it back in. An 8 × 8 inch dish works well.

Suet crust: While the pot releases, mix the self-raising flour, cornflour, shredded suet, optional dried thyme and salt with the milk to a lump-free batter — this is a poured, forgotten-style suet crust, not a rolled pastry. Spoon or pour it over the filling in the dish.

Bake: Heat the oven to 170°C fan / 190°C conventional. The host talks about 20–25 minutes; the description says 25–30. Bake until the top is risen and golden — it can bubble over a little, and the underside of the crust should be a bit soft where it has absorbed the gravy. Serve with peas if you like.

recipes.title: EASY ONE Pan BBQ Chicken Chilli
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can cannellini beans, not drained
1 (15 oz) can of kidney beans, not drained
1 (15 oz) can pinto beans, not drained
1 tsp chipotle powder (or 1 chopped chipotle in adobo) (optional for heat)
1 tbsp butter (optional, for a silky finish)
steps: Sear the chicken: Cut the chicken breasts in half through the middle (it doesn't need to be neat). Without seasoning, sear them in a little oil until there's a good crust on both sides, then take them out and cover with foil. They will keep cooking in their own steam.
Soften the aromatics: Add a little more oil and cook the garlic and onion on a low-moderate flame, scraping up the browned bits from the chicken, just until the rawness is gone.

Add the sauce: Turn the flame right down and stir in the BBQ sauce, ketchup, about 1½ tablespoons of brown sugar, about 2 tablespoons of apple cider vinegar, about 2 tablespoons of Worcestershire sauce, the liquid smoke and about 2 teaspoons of yellow mustard (Dijon also works). Stir in the spices. There's no need to bloom them, since it all stews together.

Add the beans: Add the cannellini, pinto (or chilli) and kidney beans with their liquid, undrained (drain and rinse them if you prefer), plus the chopped jalapeño. Add just a little chicken stock so the sauce stays thick.
Simmer: Bring it to the boil, then turn it down and simmer uncovered for about 25 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the chicken: Shred the chicken with two forks (leftover or rotisserie chicken also works), stir it in and simmer about 20 minutes more, stirring gently, until thick. A lid is optional.
Serve: Top with cheddar, sour cream and fresh coriander, with rice, crusty bread or cornbread. You can cut the sugar by a tablespoon, but don't leave it out completely.

ingredients: 75g golden syrup (or honey for a twist)
Honey: Honey is a natural sweetener with a similar consistency to golden syrup. It may add a slightly floral taste.
Maple Syrup offers a richer, more distinct flavour and is great for a subtle difference in taste.
Corn Syrup: Light corn syrup is the closest in texture, though it lacks the caramel-like flavour of golden syrup.
Agave Nectar is a healthier, mild-flavoured option, but it’s a bit sweeter, so you may want to use slightly less.
Molasses: For a deeper, richer flavour, though it’s stronger and darker, use sparingly.
Brown Sugar Syrup: You can make your own by dissolving brown sugar in water and boiling it until it thickens.

recipes.title: CHIKO Roll Iconic AUSTRALIAN savoury snack
ingredients: The Chiko Roll was inspired by the Chinese spring roll.
It was first sold in 1951 under "Chicken Roll," despite not containing any chicken.
McEncroe created the Chiko Roll as a convenient, portable snack that could be quickly eaten at sporting events without needing utensils or plates.
The filling of a Chiko Roll typically includes a mixture of beef, barley, cabbage, carrots, celery, and spices.
the filling is encased in a thick, doughy wrapper, making it robust enough to withstand handling without falling apart.
Chiko Rolls are usually deep-fried, giving them a crispy exterior and a soft, savory interior.
Over the decades, the Chiko Roll has become an Australian cultural icon, often associated with casual dining and takeaway food.
